definition_zh: （天气）寒冷的；刺骨的；敏捷的；麻利的；呛人的
definition_en: said of weather that is cold enough to sting the skin, and of people who move or act quickly
core_image: 清早一股冷风咬住脸颊，人下意识加快脚步
scene: 清晨出门，冷风刮脸，你不由得缩起脖子加快脚步。The wind was nippy this morning, so she pulled her scarf up over her chin.
sceneCN: 这里 nippy 是「（天气）寒冷的」（第 1 个义项：空气冷得刺人）；句意：今天早上风很冷，她把围巾拉到下巴上面。

collocations.zh: 冷得像被咬了一口（俏皮说法）

derivatives.zh: 由动词 nip（钳、咬、掐）反向构成形容词，义为「像被咬了一口那样冷」
nip 的三单形式，也指「小口喝；一小杯酒」
钳子；咬人的东西；英国口语指小孩
非本词派生；仅提示 -y 词尾常见于形容词行列，注意不要与 nippy 混淆

senses.title: Cold enough to sting the face
senses.definition: describing weather or air that is cold in a biting, sharp way
senses.definitionCN: 形容天气或空气冷得刺人、扎脸
senses.example: It was a nippy autumn evening by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 湖边的秋夜颇有寒意。
senses.why: Nip meant to bite or pinch, and nippy extends that bite to the air itself.
senses.whyCN: nip 本义是「咬、捏」，加 -y 后把「咬」的动作延伸到空气上：冷得像被咬了一口。

senses.title: Quick and lively
senses.definition: moving or working quickly and neatly, often said of a small car or of a person
senses.definitionCN: 行动或做事又快又利索，常形容小巧的汽车或人
senses.example: She is a nippy little player and covers the court in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个敏捷的小个子球员，几秒钟就能跑遍全场。
senses.why: The same bite can describe a snapping, efficient movement, so a nippy car or player is one that bites into the road or the game.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「咬住、钳住」的意象也能形容利落的动作，于是 nippy 的车或球员就像一口咬住路面或比赛。

senses.title: Biting to the tongue or nose
senses.definition: describing a sharp smell or taste that stings the mouth or nose
senses.definitionCN: 形容气味或味道尖锐刺鼻、扎嘴
senses.example: The sauce is nippy, so just a spoonful is enough.
senses.exampleCN: 那酱汁很冲，一勺就够。
senses.why: Biting is felt in the tongue as well as on the skin, so a nippy sauce bites the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 「咬」的感觉不只落在皮肤上，也会落在舌头上，所以呛人的酱汁就像在咬舌头。

senses.title: Sour and slightly sharp in flavour
senses.definition: having a lightly sharp, refreshing tang, said mostly of cheese or fruit
senses.definitionCN: 带有轻微尖锐、清爽的酸味，多用于奶酪或水果
senses.example: This cheese is nippy enough to cut through the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪味道挺冲，正好配面包。
senses.why: A mild version of the biting taste sense is used for foods with a lively tang.
senses.whyCN: 刺口义项的轻度版本被用来形容带劲儿的食物，于是有了「微酸爽口」的意思。

senses.title: Said of someone quick to snap
senses.definition: describing a person who is quick to make a sharp or impatient remark
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人说话很快、扎人或显得不耐烦
senses.example: His reply was nippy, but he was only tired.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答有点冲，不过他只是累了。
senses.why: A personality can bite as speech, so the same word moves from cold air to a sharp-tongued mood.
senses.whyCN: 性格也能用「咬」的方式表现出来，话语就会扎人，于是这个词从冷空气移到了坏脾气上。

intro.en: Nippy is the adjective from nip, a verb of obscure origin meaning to pinch or bite, with -y added in the sense of having that quality.
intro.cn: nippy 由动词 nip（掐、咬）加形容词词尾 -y 构成，nip 的来源不确定，一般认为与「捏、咬」小动物或手指动作的拟声、方言用法有关。

items.en: Nip first appears meaning to pinch, bite, or snip, and its exact origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 nip 首见时意为「掐、咬、剪」，确切来源不确定，一般认为来自低地日耳曼语族方言。

items.en: Northern dialects give nip the sense of a sharp bite of cold air.
items.cn: 苏格兰与英格兰北部方言把 nip 用来形容冷空气的「咬人」。

items.en: Nipping describes weather that stings, and a drink that nips the tongue.
items.cn: 十六世纪 nipping 开始形容刺人的天气与辣舌的饮料。

items.en: The adjective nippy is recorded for cold air and for sharp tastes.
items.cn: 十七世纪记录到形容词 nippy，用于冷空气和刺口味道。

items.en: Later British use gives nippy the meaning quick and lively, from the same biting idea.
items.cn: 后来的英式口语把 nippy 引申为「敏捷、利索」，仍沿用「咬住」的意象。

items.en: Today the word is friendly and informal, most often heard in weather talk.
items.cn: 如今这个词轻松而口语，最常出现在谈论天气的场景里。

note.en: Nippy sits in the family of nip and nipper and is close in meaning to chilly, brisk, and snappy.
note.cn: nippy 属于 nip、nipper 这一家族，意思上与 chilly、brisk、snappy 相近。

entries.definition: to pinch or bite lightly
a tool that grips things, or a small child
quick and lively, or short and sharp
entries.definitionCN: 利落的；急促的，与 nippy 只是词尾相邻，词源不同

entries.definition: cold in an unpleasant way
cold and fresh, or quick in action
very cold, with frost, or unfriendly

normalIntro.en: Nippy is the bite of nip turned into an adjective: something that nips has a nip in it.
normalIntro.cn: nippy 就是把 nip 的「咬」变成形容词：会咬人的东西身上都带一股咬劲。

normal.en: Nip means a small bite, so a nippy day is one that bites your face.
normal.cn: nip 是小口咬，所以 nippy 的日子就是会咬你脸的日子。

normal.en: The pattern is nip plus -y, and -y means having the quality of.
normal.cn: 构词规律是 nip 加 -y，-y 表示「具有……性质」。

normal.en: Say it was a nippy morning on a park walk and feel the cold.
normal.cn: 想象清晨在公园散步时说「一个冷飕飕的早晨」，感受那股冷。

normal.en: A nippy little car is the same word as a nippy morning: both are quick and sharp.
normal.cn: 「灵巧的小车」和「寒冷的清晨」用同一个词：都又快又利。

normal.en: Compare chilly, which is milder: nippy usually means a sharper, brisker cold.
normal.cn: 对比 chilly：chilly 温和一些，nippy 通常更刺、更清冷。

abstract.en: Imagine invisible tiny jaws in the wind nibbling your cheeks.
abstract.cn: 想象风里藏着看不见的小嘴，一下一下啃着你的脸颊。

abstract.en: Picture a small car darting between parked trucks like a fish.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆小车像鱼一样在停着的卡车之间穿梭。

abstract.en: Feel a drop of sharp sauce on the tongue and count to three.
abstract.cn: 想象舌尖滴上一滴带劲的酱汁，然后在心里数到三。

examples.en: It will be nippy by the coast tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚海边会很冷。

examples.en: Her little scooter is nippy in the city traffic.
examples.cn: 她的小踏板车在市区车流里很灵巧。

examples.en: The air was nippy and the leaves were already falling.
examples.cn: 空气清冷，树叶已经开始飘落。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你披」——天冷得你要披上外套，这就是 nippy；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: nip（掐、咬，来源不确定）+ -y（具有……性质）→ nippy，核心义「像被咬了一口那样的冷与利」。

sensesIntro.en: Nippy starts from the biting cold of the air, then spreads to quick movements, sharp tastes, and finally a sharp-tongued mood.
sensesIntro.cn: nippy 从空气咬人的寒冷出发，扩展到敏捷的动作、刺口的味道，最后落到说话扎人的脾气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cold wind that nips the skin like tiny teeth.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷风像小牙齿一样咬住皮肤。

branches.en: Biting weather is the most frequent sense today.
branches.cn: 「寒冷刺骨」是今天最常见的义项。

branches.en: Biting as quickness gives the lively movement sense.
branches.cn: 把「咬」理解为快速利落，就得到敏捷义。

branches.en: A smell that bites the nose is the sharp odour sense.
branches.cn: 气味咬住鼻子，就是呛鼻义。

branches.en: A milder bite on the tongue becomes a tangy taste.
branches.cn: 在舌头上轻轻的「咬」，就是微酸带劲的味道。

branches.en: A person can be nippy in body and in manner, quick and cutting at once.
branches.cn: 人既可以在身形上敏捷，也可以在言辞上扎人，两者都是「快而利」。

intro.en: Nippy is built from the verb nip plus the adjective suffix -y, and shares its family with nipper and nipping.
intro.cn: nippy 由动词 nip 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，与 nipper、nipping 同属一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Nip has no certain Latin ancestor; it is generally related to Germanic forms and is best treated as of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: nip 没有确定的拉丁语祖先，一般认为与日耳曼语族的「捏、掐」词形有关，宜标注为来源不确定。

items.example: The dog nipped my ankle.
items.exampleCN: 那只狗轻咬了我的脚踝。

items.example: The suffix -y turns nip into nippy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 nip 变成 nippy。

items.example: Nipping wind bites the ears.
items.exampleCN: 刺骨的风咬着耳朵。

items.meaning: a person or tool that does the action
items.example: The suffix -er forms nipper.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 nipper。

items.meaning: a close result in a race
items.example: The final race was nip and tuck.
items.exampleCN: 决赛难分胜负。

items.example: They nipped the rumour in the bud.
items.exampleCN: 他们早早制止了谣言。

items.example: Nippy keeps the biting image.
items.exampleCN: nippy 保留了「咬人」的意象。

items.example: A nipping breeze crossed the square.
items.exampleCN: 刺骨的微风穿过广场。

items.example: Tipsy shares the -y ending but not the word family.
items.exampleCN: tipsy 与 nippy 共有 -y 词尾，却不是同一词族。

items.example: Snappy looks close but has a different root.
items.exampleCN: snappy 看似相近，词源却不同。

definition_zh: 夜间活动的；夜行的；夜晚发生的；夜间的
definition_en: active or happening at night, especially of animals, or belonging to the night
core_image: 天黑之后猫头鹰睁圆眼睛，从枝头滑进夜色
scene: 白天睡觉，月亮一升就从树洞里钻出来去找吃的。Owls are nocturnal hunters, so you rarely see them before dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 nocturnal 是「夜间活动的」（第 1 个义项：动物在夜里活动）；句意：猫头鹰是夜行猎手，所以黄昏前很少见到它们。

pos.zh: （音乐）夜曲风格的；属于梦幻夜晚的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 nocturnal 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「在夜间地」
由 nocturnal 加名词词尾 -ity 构成，指「夜行性」这一生态特征
同源于拉丁语 nocturnus，指肖邦式的「夜曲」或「夜景画」
同源词，天主教夜间祈祷的「夜祷」，与夜间相关

senses.title: Active at night
senses.definition: said of animals that are awake and active after dark and rest in the day
senses.definitionCN: 形容动物天黑后活动、白天休息
senses.example: Bats are nocturnal and use sound to find food.
senses.exampleCN: 蝙蝠是夜行动物，靠声波觅食。
senses.why: Nocturnal comes from Latin nox, night, and -urnus, belonging to, so the word simply says belonging to the night.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语 nox（夜）加 -urnus（属于……的），天生就是「属于夜晚的」，于是动物的夜晚活动被直接说成 nocturnal。

senses.title: Happening at night
senses.definition: used of events, sounds, or activities that take place during the night
senses.definitionCN: 用于发生在夜里的事件、声音或活动
senses.example: The city has a busy nocturnal life of bars and clubs.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有热闹的夜间生活，酒吧和夜店林立。
senses.why: Once the word means belonging to the night, any event can borrow it, not only animals.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词表示「属于夜晚」，就不只限于动物，任何事件都可以借它来形容。

senses.title: Of the night in music and art
senses.definition: used for music and paintings that are dreamy and moody like the night
senses.definitionCN: 用于像夜晚一样幽静、梦幻的音乐与绘画
senses.example: Chopin wrote a nocturnal mood into many of his pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 肖邦的许多作品都带着夜的情调。
senses.why: The same root gave nocturne, a night piece, so the adjective also colours works of art with a night mood.
senses.whyCN: 同一词根诞生了 nocturne（夜曲），所以形容词也用来给艺术作品染上夜的色彩。

senses.title: Of night vision or night sight
senses.definition: describing the ability to see, or the image seen, in very low light
senses.definitionCN: 形容在微弱光线下看清东西的能力或看到的景象
senses.example: These lenses give the camera nocturnal vision.
senses.exampleCN: 这些镜头让相机具有夜视能力。
senses.why: Belonging to the night extends to tools and senses that work in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 「属于夜晚」也延伸到在黑夜里运作的工具和感官上。

senses.title: Working a night shift
senses.titleCN: 夜班工作的；夜里干活的
senses.definition: said informally of people who work during the night
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指在夜间工作的人
senses.example: Nurses on nocturnal duty often sleep in the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 上夜班的护士常常下午补觉。
senses.why: People, like animals, can be described by which half of the day they belong to.
senses.whyCN: 人也像动物一样，可以用「属于哪半个昼夜」来描述，于是有了上夜班的意思。

senses.title: Dark and shadowy in feel
senses.definition: literary use for places or moods that feel dark and secret like the night
senses.definitionCN: 文学中形容地方或情绪幽暗、隐秘如夜
senses.example: The forest had a nocturnal gloom even at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在正午，那片森林也有夜一般的幽暗。
senses.why: The literary branch borrows the darkness of night to describe atmosphere and feeling.
senses.whyCN: 文学分支借夜晚的黑暗来形容氛围与感受，所以就是「夜一般幽暗」。

intro.en: Nocturnal comes from Late Latin nocturnalis, from Latin nocturnus and nox, night, a root shared with Greek nyx and English night.
intro.cn: nocturnal 来自晚期拉丁语 nocturnalis，源于拉丁语 nocturnus（夜晚的）与 nox（夜），与希腊语 nyx、英语 night 同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root nekwt means night, giving Greek nyx and Latin nox.
items.cn: 重构词根 nekwt 意为「夜晚」，衍生出希腊语 nyx 与拉丁语 nox。

items.en: Nox is night, and nocturnus means of the night.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nox 是「夜」，nocturnus 意为「夜晚的」。

items.en: The adjective nocturnalis adds a general adjectival ending.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 nocturnalis 加上通用形容词词尾，构成正式形容词。

items.en: Middle English borrows nocturn for a nightly prayer, and the adjective follows later.
items.cn: 中古英语先借入名词 nocturn 指夜祷，形容词 nocturn 的用法随后进入英语。

items.en: Modern biology fixes nocturnal to animals active at night.
items.cn: 现代生物学把 nocturnal 固定用于夜间活动的动物。

note.en: Nocturnal shares its night root with nocturne and nocturn, and stands opposite diurnal in the animal timetable.
note.cn: nocturnal 与 nocturne、nocturn 共享「夜」的词根，在动物作息上则与 diurnal 相对。

entries.definition: a short dreamy piece of music, or a night painting
a night prayer in the Catholic office
entries.definitionCN: 天主教夜间祈祷的夜祷

entries.definition: active during the day
entries.definitionCN: 昼间活动的，与 nocturnal 相对

entries.definition: happening every night
with little or no light
active at dawn and dusk

normalIntro.en: Nocturnal is night plus a Latin adjective ending; the -ct- links it to nocturne and to the English night.
normalIntro.cn: nocturnal 是「夜」加拉丁形容词词尾，其中的 -ct- 把它和 nocturne 以及英语 night 连在一起。

normal.en: Latin nox means night, and the stem noct- appears in every form.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nox 意为「夜晚」，词干 noct- 出现在所有形式里。

normal.en: The -al ending marks a formal adjective, as in natural or national.
normal.cn: -al 是正式形容词词尾，natural、national 都是同一模式。

normal.en: Nocturne is a night piece of music, so nocturnal is simply its adjective.
normal.cn: nocturne 是夜曲，那么 nocturnal 就是它的形容词。

normal.en: Say owls are nocturnal and bats are nocturnal: zoo labels to remember.
normal.cn: 记住动物园标牌上的说法：猫头鹰是夜行的，蝙蝠也是夜行的。

normal.en: Compare diurnal: nocturnal starts at the night, diurnal starts at the day.
normal.cn: 对比 diurnal：nocturnal 从夜晚开始，diurnal 从白天开始。

abstract.en: Picture a moon disk sliding over the sky like a lid on a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一轮月亮像锅盖一样滑过天空。

abstract.en: See two wide owl eyes opening after the sun goes down.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳落山后，两只睁得溜圆的猫头鹰眼睛。

abstract.en: Hear a nocturne playing softly while the city sleeps.
abstract.cn: 想象城市入睡时，一首夜曲轻轻响起。

examples.en: Most desert rodents are nocturnal to avoid the heat.
examples.cn: 大多数沙漠啮齿动物为避开炎热而在夜间活动。

examples.en: The island has a strong nocturnal tradition of street singing.
examples.cn: 这座岛有浓厚的夜间街头歌唱传统。

examples.en: Its nocturnal vision lets it hunt in near-total darkness.
examples.cn: 它的夜视能力让它几乎在漆黑中也能捕猎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺克特哪」——夜里才有「诺克特」出没；这只是把 noct 拆成谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始印欧语 nekwt（夜晚）→ 拉丁语 nox、nocturnus（夜晚的）→ 晚期拉丁语 nocturnalis → 英语 nocturnal，核心义「属于夜晚的」。

sensesIntro.en: Nocturnal begins with the animal that belongs to the night, then widens to events, music, vision, night shifts, and the dark mood of a place.
sensesIntro.cn: nocturnal 从「属于夜晚的动物」出发，扩展到事件、音乐、夜视、夜班以及幽暗的氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an owl opening its eyes after sunset.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳落山后睁大眼睛的猫头鹰。

branches.en: Animals awake in the dark are the central sense.
branches.cn: 在黑暗里醒着的动物，是这个词的核心义项。

branches.en: Events and sounds of the night are the extended sense.
branches.cn: 夜里发生的事件与声音，是延伸义项。

branches.en: Dreamy night music and art inherit the night mood.
branches.cn: 梦幻的夜曲与夜景画继承了夜晚的情调。

branches.en: Tools that see at night and people who work at night both belong to the dark hours.
branches.cn: 夜间能看见的工具和夜间工作的人，都属于黑夜时段。

branches.en: An owl in a gloomy wood makes the dark atmosphere sense natural.
branches.cn: 幽暗树林里的猫头鹰，让「阴森幽暗」这个义项顺理成章。

intro.en: Nocturnal is built on the Latin stem noct- for night plus the adjective ending -urnus and the later -alis.
intro.cn: nocturnal 由拉丁语表「夜」的词干 noct- 加形容词词尾 -urnus 构成，后来又加了 -alis。

latinIntro.en: Latin nox, stem noct-, means night; nocturnus means of the night and nocturnalis is its later adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nox（词干 noct-）意为「夜」，nocturnus 意为「夜晚的」，nocturnalis 是较晚的形容词形式。

items.example: The stem noct- opens the word.
items.exampleCN: 词干 noct- 是这个词的开头。

items.example: Nocturnus means of the night.
items.exampleCN: nocturnus 意为属于夜晚的。

items.example: The suffix -al forms nocturnal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 nocturnal。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms nocturnally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 nocturnally。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms nocturnality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 nocturnality。

items.meaningCN: 标记名词 nocturne 的词尾
items.example: Nocturne comes through French.
items.exampleCN: nocturne 经由法语进入英语。

items.example: Diurnal is built on dies, day.
items.exampleCN: diurnal 由 dia 的变体与「日」构成。

items.example: Nocturnal keeps the night meaning.

items.example: Nocturnally active insects hide by day.
items.exampleCN: 夜间活动的昆虫白天躲起来。

items.meaning: the day and night of equal length

latinEntries.meaning: a night office or night piece

definition_zh: 名义上的；有名无实的；象征性的（费用）；记名的；名词性的
definition_en: existing in name only, very small in amount, or relating to a name or a noun
core_image: 一扇门挂着漂亮的招牌，门后却只有一间空屋
scene: 她穿着经理的牌子，可真正拍板的却是坐在隔壁的另一个人。She has the nominal title of manager, but her assistant makes all the decisions.
sceneCN: 这里 nominal 是「名义上的」（第 1 个义项：只有名分，没有实权）；句意：她挂着经理的名义头衔，但所有决定都是她的助手做的。

derivatives.zh: 由 nominal 加 -ly 构成，义为「名义上地；名义而言」
由 nominal 加动词词尾 -ize 构成，义为「使名词化」
同源于拉丁语 nominare（命名），义为「提名；任命」
同源动词，义为「提名；指定」，与「名字」的意象一脉相承

senses.title: Existing in name only
senses.definition: said of a role or status that is named but carries no real power
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个职位或身份只有名分，却没有实权
senses.example: The king was only the nominal head of the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 国王只是委员会名义上的首脑。
senses.why: Nomen is Latin for name, so nominal reaches back to the name that a thing carries rather than what it really is.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nomen 意为「名字」，所以 nominal 只指向一个东西所挂的名字，而不指向它真实的样子。

senses.title: Very small, just as a token
senses.definition: said of a price or amount that is tiny, often charged only to make an exchange official
senses.definitionCN: 形容价格或金额极小，往往只为让交易在名义上成立而收取
senses.example: The club charges a nominal fee for the class.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部只收一点象征性的课程费。
senses.why: A nominal sum is one that exists in name more than in value, so it becomes a token amount.
senses.whyCN: 名义上的金额就是「名义上存在、价值上几乎不存在」的金额，于是引申为象征性收费。

senses.title: Relating to a name
senses.definition: used for records, payments, or accounts that are held under a stated name
senses.definitionCN: 用于以某个名字登记持有的记录、款项或账户
senses.example: The shares were issued in a nominal form.
senses.exampleCN: 这些股份以记名形式发行。
senses.why: When the name is the point, the word returns to its literal link with naming and registration.
senses.whyCN: 当「名字」本身成为重点时，这个词就回到命名与登记的本义。

senses.title: Grammatical: noun-like
senses.definition: used in grammar for words or groups that work like nouns
senses.definitionCN: 语法中指像名词一样起作用的词或词组
senses.example: Noun phrases often serve as nominal subjects.
senses.exampleCN: 名词短语常充当名词性主语。
senses.why: Grammar borrows nomen again: the nominal part of a sentence is the part named like a noun.
senses.whyCN: 语法再次借用了 nomen：句子里的名词性成分就是像名词那样被「命名」的部分。

senses.title: In economics, unadjusted for inflation
senses.definition: describing money amounts at current prices, without removing inflation
senses.definitionCN: 描述按当前价格计算的金额，未剔除通货膨胀
senses.example: Wages rose in nominal terms but fell in real terms.
senses.exampleCN: 工资在名义上上涨，实际却下降了。
senses.why: A figure that only looks right on paper is nominal, as opposed to a real figure that reflects buying power.
senses.whyCN: 只在纸面上成立的数字就是名义的，与反映购买力的实际数字相对。

senses.title: Stated on the surface of a value
senses.definition: said of the printed value on a coin, note, or share rather than its market price
senses.definitionCN: 指硬币、纸币或股票票面标明的价值，而非市场价格
senses.example: The bond is trading below its nominal value.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券的交易价低于票面价值。
senses.why: The printed number is the name of the value, so it is the nominal one.
senses.whyCN: 印在票面上的数字就是这笔价值「挂的名字」，所以称为票面价值。

intro.en: Nominal comes from Latin nominalis, from nomen, a name, and reaches English through French, keeping the idea of something that exists in name.
intro.cn: nominal 来自拉丁语 nominalis，根源是 nomen（名字），经法语进入英语，始终围绕「名义」这一概念。

items.en: A reconstructed root for name lies behind Latin nomen and Greek onoma.
items.cn: 重构的「名字」词根是拉丁语 nomen 与希腊语 onoma 的共同来源。

items.en: Nomen means a name, and nominalis means of a name.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nomen 意为「名字」，nominalis 意为「名字的」。

items.en: Nominal comes into French from the Latin adjective.
items.cn: nominal 这个拉丁形容词进入法语。

items.en: English borrows nominal for matters of name and title.
items.cn: 英语借入 nominal，用于与名称、头衔有关的事。

items.en: Modern usage adds the small-fee and the economics sense of nominal values.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了「象征性费用」以及经济学中的「名义价值」。

note.en: Nominal belongs to the nomen family with nominate and nomination, and is often paired against real or actual.
note.cn: nominal 与 nominate、nomination 同属 nomen 家族，常与 real、actual 对照使用。

normalIntro.en: Nominal is the adjective of nomen, the Latin name: if something exists only in name, it is nominal.
normalIntro.cn: nominal 是拉丁语 nomen（名字）的形容词：只存在于名字里，就是名义上的。

normal.en: Nominal, nominate, and nomination all hang on the Latin name, nomen.
normal.cn: nominal、nominate、nomination 都挂在拉丁语「名字」nomen 上。

normal.en: The -al ending marks an adjective, as in normal or formal.
normal.cn: -al 是形容词词尾，normal、formal 都是同一模式。

normal.en: A nominal fee is one that exists on paper more than in practice.
normal.cn: nominal fee 是「纸面上比实际上更像回事」的费用。

normal.en: Nominal and real are a pair in economics: nominal prices, real buying power.
normal.cn: 经济学里 nominal 与 real 是一对：名义价格，实际购买力。

normal.en: Nominally is the adverb, used for roles that are only on paper.
normal.cn: 副词 nominally 常用来形容只在纸面成立的职位。

abstract.en: Picture a shiny office sign in front of an empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象一块闪亮的办公室招牌，背后却是一间空屋。

abstract.en: See a price tag marked with a tiny coin by the door.
abstract.cn: 想象门口的价签上只画了一枚很小的硬币。

abstract.en: Hold a banknote and trace its printed number with a finger.
abstract.cn: 想象手里握着一张钞票，用手指划过它印着的数字。

examples.en: She is the nominal owner, but the farm is run by her cousin.
examples.cn: 她是名义上的主人，但农场由她的表亲经营。

examples.en: Tickets cost a nominal amount of money.
examples.cn: 门票只收很少的一点钱。

examples.en: In real as well as nominal terms, the firm grew.
examples.cn: 无论按实际还是名义计算，公司都增长了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹名儿」——只闹了个名儿，没有实际内容，这就是 nominal；仅为谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始印欧语「名字」词根 → 拉丁语 nomen（名字）→ nominalis（名字的）→ 古法语 nominal → 英语 nominal，核心义「只与名字有关」。

sensesIntro.en: Nominal begins with a role that exists only in name, moves to token sums and named records, then to grammar and economics.
sensesIntro.cn: nominal 从「只有名分的职位」出发，转向象征性金额与记名记录，再进入语法学和经济学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign on a door with nothing real behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：门上挂着招牌，门后却什么也没有。

branches.en: A title with no power is the core sense.
branches.cn: 只有头衔没有实权，是核心义项。

branches.en: A name more than a value gives the small-fee sense.
branches.cn: 有名无实的价格，就是象征性收费义。

branches.en: Being held under a name is the registration sense.
branches.cn: 以名字持有，是记名义。

branches.en: Grammarians reuse the name idea for noun-like words.
branches.cn: 语法学家借「名字」来描述像名词一样的成分。

branches.en: Token sums, paper prices, and printed values all live on the surface rather than in real worth.
branches.cn: 象征性金额、账面价格与票面价值，都停留在表面而非真实价值上。

intro.en: Nominal is built on the Latin name root nomin- plus the adjective ending -al, with nominal and nominalize around it.
intro.cn: nominal 由拉丁语「名字」词根 nomin- 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，周围还有 nominalize 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen means name, and nominalis means relating to a name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nomen 意为「名字」，nominalis 意为「与名字有关的」。

items.exampleCN: nominalis 是直接来源。

definition_zh: 提名；推荐；任命；指定；命名；下注登记（赛马）
definition_en: to put a person forward for a job, prize or election, or to name someone as having done something
core_image: 桌上两份名单，有人把一个名字写进名单的空格
scene: 班里选代表，老师让同学把自己的名字写在黑板下沿。We were asked to nominate one classmate for the school debate team.
sceneCN: 这里 nominate 是「提名、推荐」（第 1 个义项：把某人提名为候选人）；句意：老师让我们提名一位同学参加校辩论队。名字一旦写上名单，那个人就进入了待推举的状态。

collocations.zh: 提名某人参加（角逐）某奖项或职位

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「提名；任命」
由 nominate 加上 -ive 构成，语法义为「主格的」，即标明动作主体的格
由动词加 -or（做事者）构成，义为「提名者」
同出拉丁语 nomen，义为「名义上的；字面的」
前缀 de- 加 nominate，义为「给……命名；以某单位标价」

senses.title: To put forward as a candidate
senses.definition: to formally suggest a person for an elected post, a prize, or a selection
senses.definitionCN: 正式提议某人出任选举职位、角逐奖项或参加遴选
senses.example: Two members nominated her for the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 两名成员提名她担任主席。
senses.why: Latin nomen means name, so nominating is placing a person on the list of names before a choice is made.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nomen 意为名字，提名就是把一个名字放进待选的名单里，供人挑选。

senses.title: To appoint to a post
senses.definition: to officially name someone to an office or position, often by one person with power
senses.definitionCN: 正式指定某人担任职务，常由掌握权力的人作出
senses.example: The board nominated him as the new treasurer.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会任命他为新的司库。
senses.why: The same act of naming becomes appointment when the namer has the power to give the post.
senses.whyCN: 同一种写名字的动作，若动作发出者有权授予职位，就不只是推荐，而成了任命。

senses.title: To name for an honour
senses.titleCN: 提名为获奖或入选人选
senses.definition: to be named as a possible winner or chosen member of a competition, list, or honour
senses.definitionCN: 被列为比赛或入选名单的候选者，可能获奖或被选中
senses.example: The film was nominated for three awards.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片获得三项大奖提名。
senses.why: Awards keep a list of names, and a nomination means the name has reached that list.
senses.whyCN: 评奖各有候选名单，被提名就是名字进入了那份名单，尚待最终揭晓。

senses.title: To specify for a purpose
senses.definition: to state that a particular person, place, or thing is to be used for a given purpose
senses.definitionCN: 指明某人、某地或某物用于某个特定用途
senses.example: Each office must nominate a person for fire drills.
senses.exampleCN: 每个办公室都必须指定一名消防演练负责人。
senses.why: Specifying is putting a name on a task, so the name marks who is assigned to the purpose.
senses.whyCN: 指定就是把名字和一件事绑在一起，名字落在哪项任务上，人就负责哪项任务。

senses.title: To name or entitle
senses.definition: to give a name to a thing, or to state what it is to be called
senses.definitionCN: 给某物取名，或说明它应当叫什么
senses.example: The villagers nominate the lake after the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们用山的名字为这个湖命名。
senses.why: The plain sense of nomen is simply a name, so the verb can mean giving one.
senses.whyCN: nomen 的本义就是名字，所以动词最朴素的用法就是给人或物一个名字。

senses.title: To enter for a race
senses.definition: to enter a horse in a race so that it is listed among the runners
senses.definitionCN: 把马匹登记进赛事，使其出现在参赛名单中
senses.example: They nominated the mare for the following day.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给这匹母马报了第二天的比赛。
senses.why: Race day has an entry list, and a nominated horse is one whose name stands on it.
senses.whyCN: 赛马有参赛登记簿，被提名的马就是名字已经写进登记簿的那匹马。

senses.title: To put on record as
senses.definition: used in informal speech to say that something belongs to a stated group or kind
senses.definitionCN: 用于口语，把某人或某物归入所说的那一类
senses.example: Put me down as nominating the budget talk as the longest.
senses.exampleCN: 我可以说，预算讨论是我见过最长的会。
senses.why: Record keeping means writing a name beside a fact, which is how a label can be put on a thing.
senses.whyCN: 记录就是在事实旁边写下名字，因而口语里可以用它表示把某物「正式算作」某一类。

senses.title: To designate an event
senses.definition: to set aside a particular date or event for a stated purpose, naming it in advance
senses.definitionCN: 提前确定某个日期或活动用于特定目的并为之定名
senses.example: The council nominated a week for the clean-up.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会指定了一个清洁周。
senses.why: Naming something in advance fixes it, so a nominated week is one that has been marked out by name.
senses.whyCN: 预先为日期或活动定名，就把它固定了下来，被指定的那一周因此有了确定的名字。

intro.en: Nominate goes back to Latin nomen, name, through the adjective nominalis, which meant relating to names.
intro.cn: nominate 可追溯到拉丁语 nomen（名字），经形容词 nominalis（与名称有关的）进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root often written no-men meant name.
items.cn: 构拟词根常写作 no-men，意为名字。

items.en: Nomen means name, and the adjective nominalis means belonging to a name.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nomen 意为名字，形容词 nominalis 意为与名称有关的。

items.en: The verb comes from Latin nominare, to name, as borrowed through scholarly use.
items.cn: 动词来自拉丁语 nominare（命名、提名），经学术用语进入英语。

items.en: Nominate is first used for the act of naming or appointing an officer.
items.cn: nominate 最早用于指为官职命名或任命人选的行为。

items.en: The word spreads into elections, awards, races, and everyday speech.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到选举、评奖、赛马以及日常口语。

items.en: Nomination is the fixed noun, and nominal keeps the literal sense of name.
items.cn: 名词固化使用 nomination，而 nominal 保留了「名义的」这一字面义。

note.en: Nominate shares its root with nominal and nominative, and is close in meaning to propose, appoint, and designate.
note.cn: nominate 与 nominal、nominative 同出「名字」这一词根，意义上与 propose、appoint、designate 相邻。

existing in name only, or relating to a name

entries.definitionCN: 语法中的主格，即为主语命名的那一格

to choose someone officially for a job
to officially choose someone or something for a purpose

normalIntro.en: Nominate carries Latin nomen, name, so each meaning is a way of writing a name in the right place.
normalIntro.cn: nominate 带着拉丁语 nomen（名字），所以每个义项都是把名字写到合适的位置上。

normal.en: Nominate a candidate means to put a name forward for a choice.
normal.cn: nominate a candidate 就是把一个名字推出去供大家选。

normal.en: Nominate someone as manager is to appoint them by name.
normal.cn: nominate someone as manager 就是按名字任命其为经理。

normal.en: Compare nomination: the noun keeps exactly the same name image.
normal.cn: 对比名词 nomination，它保留的正是同一个「名字」意象。

normal.en: Nominal means in name only, showing the plain sense of nomen.
normal.cn: nominal 意为只是名义上的，显示出 nomen 最朴素的含义。

normal.en: In elections, nominate comes before vote, because names come before choice.
normal.cn: 在选举里先 nominate 再 vote，因为名字总在挑选之前。

abstract.en: Picture a list of names and a hand adding one more line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张候选名单，一只手在上面添了一个名字。

abstract.en: Imagine a name set in gold on a prize envelope.
abstract.cn: 想象名字被印成金色，写在一个颁奖信封上。

abstract.en: See a clipboard outside a door with one name clipped to it.
abstract.cn: 想象门口挂着一块写字板，上面夹着一个人名。

examples.en: Our union will nominate two members for the safety committee.
examples.cn: 我们工会将提名两名成员进入安全委员会。

examples.en: She was nominated for a national teaching prize and won it.
examples.cn: 她获得了一项全国教学奖提名，并最终获奖。

examples.en: The club nominated a day in June for the clean-up.
examples.cn: 俱乐部把六月的一天定为大扫除日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹米内推」——内推就是把人推进提名名单，记住这层联想即可，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 nomen（名字）→ 形容词 nominalis（与名称有关的）→ 拉丁语 nominare（命名、提名）→ 英语 nominate，核心义「把名字写到名单上」。

sensesIntro.en: Nominate starts from writing a name on a list, widens to appointing and awarding, and loosens into naming a date or labelling a thing in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: nominate 从把名字写进名单出发，扩展到任命与评奖，再放宽为指定日期与口语中的归类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leader placing a name on a list of candidates.
core.cn: 核心意象：领导者把一个名字写进候选名单。

branches.en: Putting a name forward is the list sense.
branches.cn: 把名字推出去，是名单式的义项。

branches.en: Naming a person for a post or a week for an event fixes it by authority.
branches.cn: 凭权力为人定岗、为活动定期，都是把名字钉在这些事上。

branches.en: The prize shortlist is the public face of the list image.
branches.cn: 奖项候选名单是「名单」意象最公开的一面。

branches.en: Specifying a role attaches a name to a job.
branches.cn: 指定职责，就是把名字贴到一件工作上。

branches.en: Giving a name, entering a horse, and labelling in speech all keep the plain nomen sense.
branches.cn: 命名、赛马登记与口语归类，都保留了 nomen 的本义。

intro.en: Nominate is built on the Latin root nomen, name, with the suffix -ate forming a verb and -ion forming the noun.
intro.cn: nominate 建在拉丁词根 nomen（名字）之上，后缀 -ate 构成动词，-ion 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen means name, and nominare means to call by name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nomen 意为名字，nominare 意为叫出名字、命名。

items.example: Nomen is the root of nominate.
items.exampleCN: nomen 是 nominate 的词根。

items.example: The suffix -ate makes verbs such as nominate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 nominate 这类动词。

items.example: The stem nomin- appears in nominal and nomination.
items.exampleCN: 词干 nomin- 出现在 nominal 和 nomination 里。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词
items.example: Nomination adds -ion to the verb.
items.exampleCN: nomination 在动词后加 -ion。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示具有某种作用或性质的形容词
items.example: The case nominative marks the subject by name.
items.exampleCN: 主格 nominative 用名字标出动作主体。

items.example: Nominator is the person who nominates.
items.exampleCN: nominator 就是提名的人。

items.meaning: to name, to give a unit
items.meaningCN: 命名；（货币）以某单位标值
items.example: To denominate a coin is to give it a name.
items.exampleCN: 给硬币 denominated，就是给它一个单位名称。

items.example: Nominal means relating to names only.
items.exampleCN: nominal 指只在名称上成立。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a name
items.example: Latin nominalis leads to the English adjective nominal.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 nominalis 引出英语形容词 nominal。

definition_zh: 禁止吸烟的（区域或规定）；不吸烟的（人）
definition_en: used to describe a place where smoking is forbidden, or a person who does not smoke
core_image: 灰暗的食堂被划成两半，左边挂起一块禁烟的牌子
scene: 餐厅老板把靠窗的一排桌子改成无烟区，桌上立着小牌子。The owner marked the window seats as a nonsmoking area for families.
sceneCN: 这里 nonsmoking 是「禁止吸烟的」（第 1 个义项：区域或场合不允许吸烟）；句意：店主把靠窗的座位划为供家庭使用的禁烟区。一句话就把整片空间从「可以吸烟」改成「不允许吸烟」。

pos.zh: 禁烟（用作定语或口语说法）；不吸烟的状态

derivatives.zh: 由 nonsmoking 加 -er 构成，义为「不吸烟的人」
去掉否定前缀 non- 的基本词，义为「吸烟者」
改用抗性前缀 anti-，义为「反吸烟的、禁烟的」
以 -free（没有）构成的同义表达，义为「无烟的」

senses.title: Not allowing smoking
senses.definition: describing a room, building, or area where smoking is not permitted
senses.definitionCN: 形容不允许吸烟的房间、建筑或场所
senses.example: All of the second floor is a nonsmoking area.
senses.exampleCN: 整层二层都是禁烟区。
senses.why: The prefix non- simply adds not, so nonsmoking first of all means the act of smoking is not present.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 non- 只表示「不」，所以最早的意思就是这里不发生吸烟这个动作，单纯一个「不」字贴在整个空间上。

senses.title: A person who does not smoke
senses.definition: used of a person who never or rarely smokes
senses.definitionCN: 形容从不吸烟或很少吸烟的人
senses.example: She prefers a nonsmoking flatmate.
senses.exampleCN: 她更愿意找一位不吸烟的室友。
senses.why: When non- attaches to a person, the same not marks a habit rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 当 non- 贴在一个人身上，同样一个「不」就由场所限制变成了生活习惯的描述。

senses.title: A rule against smoking
senses.definition: a policy or rule that forbids smoking in a place, often attached to the word policy
senses.definitionCN: 禁止在某个场合吸烟的规定或政策，常与 policy 连用
senses.example: The hospital adopted a strict nonsmoking policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院实行严格的禁烟政策。
senses.why: A written rule turns the prohibition of an area into a thing that can be adopted and enforced.
senses.whyCN: 写下来的条文把某个空间的禁令变成可以采纳、可以执行的对象，于是 non- 落到一条政策上。

senses.title: Smoke-free by construction
senses.definition: describing accommodation or facilities that are built or designated to be free of smoke
senses.definitionCN: 形容按设计或规定设为没有烟雾的客房与设施
senses.example: They booked a nonsmoking room with two beds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们订了一间带两张床的无烟房。
senses.why: Hotels and airlines name an entire class of rooms this way, so the word becomes part of a product name.
senses.whyCN: 酒店和航空公司用这个词给一整类房间或座位命名，于是它从一个禁令变成了产品的标签。

senses.title: The opposite of smoking
senses.definition: forming the negative term for a habit, condition, or activity, as in nonsmoking and nondrinking
senses.definitionCN: 构成与某种习惯或行为相对的否定说法，如不吸烟、不饮酒
senses.example: The clinic lists exercise and nonsmoking as equal goals.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把锻炼和不吸烟列为同等重要的目标。
senses.why: Non- works as a plain opposite-forming prefix, so the word can pair with any habit it negates.
senses.whyCN: non- 的作用就是把一个习惯反过来，所以它能和任何同类习惯并列，构成一组彼此呼应的否定说不。

senses.title: Implying a rule of the premises
senses.definition: used to warn people that smoking will be refused, as on a sign at an entrance
senses.definitionCN: 用于提醒进入者这里会拒绝吸烟，如入口处的告示
senses.example: A small nonsmoking sign hangs above the lift.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯上方挂着一块小小的禁烟标志。
senses.why: A sign is the shortest form of a prohibition, so the word becomes an alert before anyone lights up.
senses.whyCN: 告示是一条禁令最短的形式，所以这个词落在牌子上时，成了在别人点烟之前先给出的警告。

intro.en: Nonsmoking is a modern compound: the prefix non-, meaning not, added to the English verb and noun smoke.
intro.cn: nonsmoking 是现代英语的复合词：否定前缀 non-（不）加上英语动词与名词 smoke。

items.en: Latin non is simply the word for not.
items.cn: 拉丁语 non 就是「不」这个字。

items.en: Non- becomes an English prefix that makes opposites such as nonsense.
items.cn: non- 成为英语前缀，用来构成 nonsense 这类反义或否定词。

items.en: Smoke goes back to Old English smocian, to smoke, related to smeocan, to emit smoke.
items.cn: smoke 可追溯到古英语 smocian（吸烟），与 smeocan（冒烟）同源。

items.en: Public health campaigns turn the prefix and the word into a fixed label.
items.cn: 公共健康运动把前缀与词根连成一个固定的标签。

items.en: Nonsmoking appears as a compound label for areas and for people in the 1900s.
items.cn: 到了二十世纪，nonsmoking 成为形容区域与人的固定复合标签。

items.en: Signs, hotel rooms, and seating sections spread the compound worldwide.
items.cn: 告示牌、酒店客房与座位分区把这套复合词推广到全世界。

note.en: Nonsmoking is a non- compound whose nearest relatives are nonsmoker, smoke-free, and anti-smoking.
note.cn: nonsmoking 是 non- 复合词，最近亲是 nonsmoker、smoke-free 与 anti-smoking。

entries.definition: a person who does not smoke
the act of using cigarettes or pipes
producing little or no smoke
free of smoking by rule or about to become so
working against the use of tobacco
without tobacco products

normalIntro.en: Nonsmoking is three pieces: non- for not, smoke for the habit, and -ing for the activity.
normalIntro.cn: nonsmoking 由三块组成：non- 表示不，smoke 表示吸烟，-ing 表示这项活动。

normal.en: The prefix non- makes a plain opposite, as in nonsense.
normal.cn: 前缀 non- 造出直白的反面说法，nonsense 就是这样来的。

normal.en: Nonsmoking area is the most common place to meet the word.
normal.cn: nonsmoking area 是这个单词最常出现的地方。

normal.en: Nonsmoker is the person; nonsmoking describes a place or a habit.
normal.cn: nonsmoker 指人，nonsmoking 形容场所或习惯。

normal.en: Smoking itself is the base word, so the negative form keeps its -ing.
normal.cn: smoking 本身就是基本词，所以否定式仍保留 -ing。

normal.en: Hotel rooms use nonsmoking as a product label, not a warning only.
normal.cn: 酒店的 nonsmoking room 是一种房型标签，而不只是警告。

abstract.en: Picture a grey cloud stopped at a glass door marked with a sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一团灰烟被一块写着标志的玻璃门挡住了。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole carriage of cleared air after the announcement.
abstract.cn: 想象广播响过之后，整节车厢变得清清爽爽。

abstract.en: See a dozen guests in hotel rooms, each choosing the clean side.
abstract.cn: 想象酒店的客房客人，纷纷选了清朗的那一侧。

examples.en: Please ask for a nonsmoking table when you book.
examples.cn: 订位时请要求禁烟区的桌子。

examples.en: The new nonsmoking rule covers the whole building.
examples.cn: 新的禁烟规定覆盖整栋大楼。

examples.en: She is a nonsmoker and wants a nonsmoking flatmate.
examples.cn: 她不吸烟，想找一位不吸烟的室友。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弄不什莫king」——记成「弄不到烟」的地方；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 non（不）+ 古英语 smocian（吸烟，与 smeocan 冒烟同源）→ smoking（吸烟）→ 加否定前缀 non- → 英语 nonsmoking，核心义「不允许吸烟」。

sensesIntro.en: Nonsmoking moves from a place that forbids smoke, to a person who does not smoke, to a written rule and a labelled product.
sensesIntro.cn: nonsmoking 先指禁止吸烟的场所，再指不吸烟的人，然后扩展到成文规定与产品标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign with a crossed-out cigarette standing beside a clean room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块画着被划掉的香烟的牌子立在一间干净的房间里。

branches.en: A room that forbids smoke is the basic place sense.
branches.cn: 禁止吸烟的房间，是最基础的场所义项。

branches.en: The same not applied to a person marks the habit sense.
branches.cn: 同一个「不」加在人身上，就得到习惯义项。

branches.en: A rule and a sign both make the prohibition public.
branches.cn: 规定与标志都是把禁令公开出来。

branches.en: Rooms sold as nonsmoking turn the ban into a product.
branches.cn: 以无烟为卖点的客房，把禁令变成了商品。

branches.en: Used beside other habits, the word shows non- as a general opposite.
branches.cn: 与其他习惯并列时，可见 non- 是一般的否定前缀。

intro.en: Nonsmoking is a modern non- compound: a Latin negative prefix, an English root, and the noun-forming -ing.
intro.cn: nonsmoking 是现代 non- 复合词：拉丁否定前缀加英语词根，再由 -ing 构成名词性成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin non means not, and it is the simplest negation in the Latin vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 non 意为不，是拉丁语中最简单的否定词。

items.example: Non- forms the opposite, as in nonsmoking.
items.exampleCN: non- 构成反义，non 加 smoking 就是禁烟。

items.example: Smoke is the root the prefix attaches to.
items.exampleCN: smoke 是前缀所挂靠的词根。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示活动或过程的名词
items.example: The suffix -ing names the activity of smoking.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 把吸烟说成一项活动。

items.example: Nonsmoker adds -er to name the person.
items.exampleCN: nonsmoker 加 -er 指人。

items.example: Anti-smoking renames the same idea as a struggle.
items.exampleCN: anti-smoking 把同一个意思说成一场对抗。

items.example: Smoke-free uses -free instead of the prefix.
items.exampleCN: smoke-free 用 -free 取代了否定前缀。

items.example: Smokeless describes a device without visible smoke.
items.exampleCN: smokeless 描述没有可见烟雾的器具。

items.example: The compound keeps the exact meaning of its parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词的含义正好由两部分相加而成。

items.meaningCN: 能自由构成否定词的前缀
items.example: Non- can attach to almost any activity noun.
items.exampleCN: non- 几乎能加在任何活动名词前面。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不是人（示例用法，说明 non 的否定功能）

definition_zh: （诉讼中）中止起诉；诉讼不成立；使诉讼被驳回；撤诉
definition_en: a court order ending a person or case from further proceedings, usually because the claim was not properly proved or pursued
core_image: 书记员在案卷首页盖上一枚红章，整摞卷宗随即合上
scene: 庭审进行到一半，原告自己的证人说法互相矛盾，法官当场宣布此案就此终结。After the witness contradicted himself, the judge ordered a nonsuit against the claimant.
sceneCN: 这里 nonsuit 是「中止诉讼、诉讼不成立」（第 2 个义项：法院在案件未能有效推进时终结程序的裁定）；句意：证人自相矛盾之后，法官下令对原告作出诉讼不成立的裁定。这是一个法律术语，多用于较旧的判例与程序记述。

pos.zh: 中止诉讼；诉讼不成立（的裁定）
中止（原告）的诉讼；使诉讼被驳回

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀 non- 与词根 suit 后的基本动词，义为「起诉；控告」
同用 suit 的法律名词，义为「诉讼」
基本词，法律义为「诉讼；起诉」
意义相近的程序用语，义为「中止（诉讼）」

senses.title: An order stopping further proceedings
senses.definition: a court order that ends the further progress of an action or of a person as plaintiff
senses.definitionCN: 法院作出的终结某项诉讼或终结某人作为原告资格的命令
senses.example: The court entered a nonsuit after the claim was abandoned.
senses.exampleCN: 原告放弃诉讼请求后，法院作出了中止诉讼的记录。
senses.why: Non- means not and suit means the legal action, so a nonsuit is quite simply a suit that is not going on.
senses.whyCN: non- 表示不，suit 表示诉讼，所以 nonsuit 字面上就是一场不再继续的诉讼，裁定只是给这个状态落了文书。

senses.title: A verdict that the claim failed
senses.definition: a judgment, often given by the judge during trial, that the plaintiff has not proved enough to continue
senses.definitionCN: 常在开庭中由法官作出的判决，认定原告证据不足、不能继续审理
senses.example: The judge ordered a nonsuit at the end of the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 证据出示完毕后，法官作出了诉讼不成立的裁定。
senses.why: The word often names the moment a judge stops a trial, so it turns the idea of a stopped suit into the ruling itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常指法官中断审理的那一刻，于是「停止的诉讼」也就成了那份终止审理的判决本身。

senses.title: To put a plaintiff out of court
senses.titleCN: 使原告中止诉讼；驳回其诉讼
senses.definition: of a court, to deprive a plaintiff of the right to continue the action
senses.definitionCN: 指法院剥夺原告继续该项诉讼的权利
senses.example: The bench nonsuited the claimant and ordered costs.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭使原告的诉讼被驳回，并判其负担诉讼费用。
senses.why: Once the noun names a stopped case, the historian of the word turns it into an act the judge performs on the plaintiff.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然已经指被停掉的案子，后来就自然转为法官对原告做的一个动作：把他的诉讼从这个法庭里撤下来。

senses.title: The recording of a withdrawal
senses.definition: a formal entry of a withdrawal of suit, which in older practice had to be made at the proper stage
senses.definitionCN: 对撤诉行为的正式登记，旧时诉讼程序要求它在恰当的阶段作出
senses.example: A plaintiff may enter a nonsuit only before the case goes to the jury.
senses.exampleCN: 原告只能在案件交由陪审团之前作撤诉登记。
senses.why: Procedure needs a written trace, so a stopped suit also becomes an entry written into the record.
senses.whyCN: 程序讲究书面痕迹，于是「停下的诉讼」又多了一层意思：写进案卷里的一条撤诉记录。

senses.title: Judgment entered against the claimant
senses.titleCN: 对原告作出的败诉判决
senses.definition: in some older systems, a judgment entered against a plaintiff who failed to attend or to complete the claim
senses.definitionCN: 在某些旧制度中，对未出庭或未完成诉讼的原告作出的判决
senses.example: Counsel moved for judgment of nonsuit on the fourth day.
senses.exampleCN: 第四天，律师申请作出诉讼不成立的判决。
senses.why: A stopped suit still has to be answered by the court, so the word can name the judgment that closes it.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼虽停，法院仍要给一个交代，因此这个词也能指那份把诉讼正式关上的判决。

senses.title: A claim that lapses
senses.titleCN: 诉讼因程序瑕疵而终止
senses.definition: a state in which the claim ends without a decision on the merits, for example through a procedural defect
senses.definitionCN: 指诉讼因程序瑕疵等而未作实体裁判即告结束的状态
senses.example: Few modern codes still use nonsuit for an abandoned claim.
senses.exampleCN: 现代法典已很少用 nonsuit 指放弃的诉讼请求。
senses.why: The core idea of a suit that does not go on shades into any case that quietly falls away for procedural reasons.
senses.whyCN: 「不再继续的诉讼」这一核心含义逐渐延伸到任何因程序原因而悄悄消失的案件。

intro.en: Nonsuit is a legal compound of non-, not, and suit, the action at law, with the noun attested from the 1500s and the verb soon after.
intro.cn: nonsuit 是法律复合词，由 non-（不）与 suit（诉讼）构成，名词据记载形成于十六世纪，动词稍后出现。

items.en: Non means not, the simplest negation in Latin.
items.cn: non 意为「不」，是拉丁语中最简单的否定词。

items.en: Suit in English law practice came through Anglo-Norman French
items.cn: 英语法律实践中的 suit 经诺曼—法语传入，指正式的诉讼请求。

items.en: The underlying Latin root is sequi, to follow, giving sue and suit the idea of pursuit.
items.cn: 更底层的拉丁词根是 sequi（跟随），让 sue 与 suit 带有「追随」的意味。

items.en: Suit is settled in law as the formal demand or action of a plaintiff.
items.cn: suit 在法律中固定为原告提出的正式请求与诉讼。

items.en: Non- is added to form a term for a stopped or abandoned action.
items.cn: 人们加上 non-，造出表示受挫或放弃的诉讼的术语。

items.en: Nonsuit survives mostly in older judgments and in the codes of some American states.
items.cn: nonsuit 主要保留在较早的判词以及美国一些州的法典中。

note.en: Nonsuit sits in the legal word family of suit, sue, and lawsuit, and is close in meaning to discontinuance and dismissal.
note.cn: nonsuit 属于 suit、sue、lawsuit 这一法律词族，意义上与 discontinuance、dismissal 相邻。

entries.definition: a legal claim brought before a court
a claim brought to a court of law
a set of connected rooms or a set of things
entries.definitionCN: 套房；一套，这里只是拼写相近，词源不同（suite 出自法语 suivre 的过去分词）

entries.definition: a judge ending a case without a full trial
the act of ending an action already begun
the decision of a court or jury at the end of a trial

normalIntro.en: Nonsuit chains non-, not, to suit, the action at law, so the whole word is a suit that does not proceed.
normalIntro.cn: nonsuit 把 non-（不）接到 suit（诉讼）前面，整个词就是一场没能继续下去的诉讼。

normal.en: Judgment of nonsuit is the standard phrase for a stopped claim.
normal.cn: judgment of nonsuit 是表示诉讼不成立的固定说法。

normal.en: Sue and suit share the idea of pursuit, so a nonsuit ends the chase.
normal.cn: sue 与 suit 都有追赶的意思，nonsuit 就是停止追击。

normal.en: Move for a nonsuit is what counsel does when the evidence is thin.
normal.cn: 证据不足时，律师会 move for a nonsuit，即申请中止诉讼。

normal.en: Nonsuit the plaintiff means the judge takes the case away from the claimant.
normal.cn: nonsuit the plaintiff 指法官把案子从原告手里拿走。

normal.en: Compare discontinuance, the ordinary word for ending an action.
normal.cn: 对比 discontinuance，那是表示中止诉讼的普通词。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk drawing a red stamp down on the case file.
abstract.cn: 想象书记员把红色印章重重按在案卷封面上。

abstract.en: See a judge lifting a paper and laying it on a closed pile.
abstract.cn: 想象法官拿起一页纸，把它放到已经合上的那一摞上。

abstract.en: Imagine a plaintiff carrying a bundle out through the court door.
abstract.cn: 想象原告抱着一摞材料，从法院门口走了出去。

examples.en: The judge ordered a nonsuit after the claimant failed to appear.
examples.cn: 原告未出庭后，法官作出了中止诉讼的裁定。

examples.en: A plaintiff who wishes to withdraw must enter a nonsuit at the proper stage.
examples.cn: 原告若想撤诉，必须在恰当阶段作撤诉登记。

examples.en: The court nonsuited the claimant and awarded costs to the defendant.
examples.cn: 法院使原告的诉讼被驳回，并判被告获得诉讼费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弄诉的」——把「诉讼」弄停、弄没了，就是中止诉讼；这只是一句谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 non（不）+ 法律用语 suit（诉讼，源自拉丁语 sequi「跟随」所生的法律「请求」义）→ 英语复合名词 nonsuit（中止诉讼），后转为动词，核心义「一场不再继续的诉讼」。

sensesIntro.en: Nonsuit starts as a ruling that stops a suit, expands to the judgment against a claimant, and settles as the formal record of a withdrawal.
sensesIntro.cn: nonsuit 最早指中止诉讼的裁定，继而扩展为对原告的败诉判决，最终也指撤诉的正式记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a court file closed with a red stamp across its cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份案卷被合上，封面上压着一枚红章。

branches.en: The basic sense is a suit that is not continued.
branches.cn: 最基本的义项就是一场不再继续的诉讼。

branches.en: Both a trial ruling and a default judgment are the court closing the case.
branches.cn: 开庭时的裁定与缺席判决，都是法院把案件关上的动作。

branches.en: The judge acting on the plaintiff is the verb side of the word.
branches.cn: 法官对原告采取行动，是这个词的动词一面。

branches.en: A withdrawal properly entered is the paper trace of the stopping.
branches.cn: 依程序作出的撤诉登记，是「停案」留下的书面痕迹。

branches.en: A lapsed claim is the stopping without any decision on the merits.
branches.cn: 诉讼因程序原因终止，是没有触及实体即告停下。

intro.en: Nonsuit is built from the negative prefix non- and the legal noun suit, with the verb formed from the noun.
intro.cn: nonsuit 由否定前缀 non- 与法律名词 suit 构成，动词则由名词转来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin behind the word is non, not, and the root sequi, to follow, which supplies the legal sense of pursuit.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁语是 non（不）与词根 sequi（跟随），后者提供了「追索」的法律含义。

items.example: Non- turns a suit into a nonsuit.
items.exampleCN: non- 把诉讼变成中止诉讼。

items.example: Suit is the noun the compound modifies.
items.exampleCN: suit 是该复合词所修饰的名词。

items.meaning: to bring a claim to court
items.example: Sue carries the same underlying root.
items.exampleCN: sue 承载同一个底层词根。

items.example: The root sequ- gives suit its sense of pursuit.
items.exampleCN: 词根 sequ- 赋予 suit 追索的含义。

items.example: Discontinuance adds dis- to the idea of stopping.
items.exampleCN: discontinuance 用 dis- 强化中断之意。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示状态或动作的名词
items.example: The suffix -ance forms discontinuance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 构成 discontinuance。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示行为的法律名词
items.example: Dismissal uses -al for the act of ending a case.
items.exampleCN: dismissal 用 -al 表示终止案件的这一行为。

items.meaning: a suit that does not proceed
items.example: The legal compound keeps the plain meaning of both parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个法律复合词保留了前后两部分的本义。

latinEntries.meaning: a following, a course of action

definition_zh: 怀旧；怀乡之情；对往昔的怀念；怀旧的商品或潮流
definition_en: a feeling of pleasure mixed with sadness when you think about the past or a place you have left
core_image: 离乡的士兵坐在窗前，手里握着一张旧照片，望着通往故乡的路
scene: 老兵翻开抽屉，看到一张发黄的全家福，久久说不出话。A wave of nostalgia swept over the old soldier as he looked at the faded family photo.
sceneCN: 这里 nostalgia 是「怀旧之情」（第 1 个义项：带着甜与苦的对往昔的怀念）；句意：望着那张褪色的全家福，一阵怀旧之情涌上老兵心头。

pos.zh: 怀旧；怀乡之情；思乡病；怀旧的商品或风气

derivatives.zh: nostalgia 加后缀 -ic 构成，怀旧的；思乡的
nostalgic 加后缀 -ally 构成，怀着怀旧之情地；怀旧地
nostalgia 加后缀 -ist 构成，好怀旧的人；怀旧者

senses.title: Longing mixed with sadness for the past
senses.titleCN: 对往昔的怀念：甜中带苦
senses.definition: a sentimental longing for a period or an experience in the past, felt as pleasure mixed with sadness
senses.definitionCN: 对过去某段时光或经历的一种感伤式向往，既带来愉悦，又夹杂哀愁
senses.example: A wave of nostalgia swept over her as she smelled the old school hall.
senses.exampleCN: 闻到旧校舍里的气味，一阵怀旧之情涌上她心头。
senses.why: Greek nostos is a homecoming and algos is pain, so the word builds pain at coming home; later that ache was turned toward any lost time.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 nostos 意为「归乡」，algos 意为「痛苦」，这个词从一开始就是「归乡之痛」；后来这份痛被引向任何一种逝去的时光。

senses.title: Homesickness
senses.definition: an intense longing to return home felt by a person who is far from it
senses.definitionCN: 远离家乡的人对回家的强烈思念
senses.example: The students described their nostalgia for family dinners in the first term.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们描述了第一学期里对家庭晚餐的思念。
senses.why: Nostalgia was coined for a medical condition of Swiss soldiers longing for home, so homesickness is its oldest and most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: nostalgia 最初是为瑞士士兵思乡的病症而造出的医学用语，因此思乡是它最古老、最字面的义项。

senses.title: Glorifying an idealized past
senses.definition: a wistful or sentimental preference for the past, often when that past is remembered as better than it really was
senses.definitionCN: 对过去的感伤偏爱，常把这段过去记得比实际情况更美好
senses.example: The essay warns against nostalgia for the golden age of cheap housing.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章提醒人们不要对廉价住房的黄金时代抱有美化的怀旧情结。
senses.why: Once the mind has been turned backwards, it tends to polish what it sees there, and the longing becomes a preference for a past that never quite existed.
senses.whyCN: 心思一旦转向过去，就会把看到的东西打磨光亮，于是怀念变成对那个并不完全存在过的过去的偏爱。

senses.title: Nostalgia as style and products
senses.definition: a fashion, style, or range of products that borrows images and sounds from an earlier decade
senses.definitionCN: 借用某个更早年代的影像与声音的时尚、风格或一系列商品
senses.example: The film relies on nostalgia for the nineties rather than on its own plot.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影靠的是对九十年代的怀旧感，而不是自身的剧情。
senses.why: When enough people feel the same longing, sellers turn it into records, clothes and songs that can be bought, so the feeling becomes a market.
senses.whyCN: 当怀旧的人足够多，商人就把它变成可以买到的唱片、衣服和歌曲，于是情感变成了市场。

intro.en: Nostalgia is a coined medical term of the seventeenth century, built from Greek nostos, homecoming, and algos, pain.
intro.cn: nostalgia 是十七世纪新造的医学术语，由希腊语 nostos（归乡）与 algos（痛苦）构成。

items.en: Greek nostos meant a return home, a word usually tied to the homeward voyages told in the Odyssey.
items.cn: 希腊语 nostos 意为「归乡」，常与「奥德赛」史诗中的归乡航行联系在一起。

items.en: Greek algos meant pain, and it supplies the second half of many medical words.
items.cn: 希腊语 algos 意为「痛苦」，它构成了许多医学术语的后半部分。

items.en: The Swiss physician Johannes Hofer coined nostalgia in Latin to name the homesickness of soldiers serving far from home.
items.cn: 瑞士医生约翰内斯·霍费尔用拉丁语造出 nostalgia，用来命名远在异乡服役的士兵的思乡病。

items.en: While it was still treated as a military illness, French doctors took the word over as nostalgie.
items.cn: 当这个词仍被当作军中医症时，法国医生把它借去，写作 nostalgie。

items.en: English borrowed nostalgia in the eighteenth century; the medical reading of homesickness faded during the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 nostalgia；把思乡当成疾病的医学解读在十九世纪逐渐消退。

items.en: In the twentieth century the sense widened from a place to any lost time, and nostalgia also names styles that borrow the past.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词的指向从某个地点扩大到任何逝去的时光，nostalgia 也开始指借用过去风格的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers members of the nostalgia word family and words that only look similar; the near-meaning group gathers other longings, their opposites, and the medical term it grew from.
note.cn: 形近组收 nostalgia 词族成员以及只是拼写相近的词；近义组收其他形式的思念、反义对照，以及它所脱胎的医学术语。

entries.definition: adjective: feeling or expressing nostalgia, or causing that feeling in others
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怀旧的、思乡的、令人怀旧的」，由本词加后缀 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: adverb: in a way that shows nostalgia
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「怀着怀旧之情地」，由 nostalgic 加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: pain along a nerve; it shares only the Greek element algos, pain, with nostalgia
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神经痛」，只与 nostalgia 共用表示「痛苦」的希腊成分 algos，整词词源不同。

entries.definition: the plain English word for longing to be back home, with no sentimental charm
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「思乡」，是朴素的日常说法，不带感伤的美化色彩。

entries.definition: a strong feeling of wanting something or someone, not tied to the past
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「渴望、思念」，泛指想要某人某事，不一定指向过去。

entries.definition: missing home while away; the everyday adjective where nostalgia is the learned noun
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「想家的」，在日常口语中代替较文雅的 nostalgia。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek parts of the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的希腊构词成分，以及它实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Nostalgia is nostos, homecoming, plus algos, pain: the ache of coming home.
normal.cn: nostalgia 是 nostos（归乡）加 algos（痛苦）：归来的那一点隐痛。

normal.en: A wave of nostalgia means the feeling arrives suddenly and passes over you like water.
normal.cn: a wave of nostalgia 意为这种感觉突然袭来，像波浪一样漫过你。

normal.en: Nostalgia for the past is the standard way to name longing for earlier times.
normal.cn: nostalgia for the past 是表达「对往昔怀念」的标准说法。

normal.en: Neurologists once treated homesickness as an illness, so nostalgia first meant a medical complaint.
normal.cn: 当年神经科医生把思乡当作一种病来治，所以 nostalgia 最初是个医学术语。

normal.en: Compare the pair: nostalgia is the noun, nostalgic is the adjective; the -algia ending is the same pain.
normal.cn: 对比这一对：nostalgia 是名词，nostalgic 是形容词；结尾的 -algia 与神经痛里的「痛」同源。

abstract.en: Picture a train window at dusk: fields rush past backwards, and the faster they move, the more tenderly you remember them.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏的车窗：田野一幕幕向后掠过，越退越快，你记得越温柔。

abstract.en: Imagine an old photograph kept in a coat pocket: the pocket is a house you carry, and the photo is the road home.
abstract.cn: 想象大衣口袋里的一张旧照片：口袋是你随身带着的家，照片是回家的路。

abstract.en: Think of a museum of one decade being built in a shopping street: the longing is turned into windows you can look into.
abstract.cn: 想象一条商业街上建起一座属于某个年代的博物馆：怀念被做成了可以张望的橱窗。

examples.en: Many older residents feel nostalgia for the quiet streets of their youth.
examples.cn: 许多年长的居民对年轻时安静的街道心怀怀念。

examples.en: His nostalgia for the village faded once he moved back for good.
examples.cn: 他彻底搬回村子之后，那份思乡之情就淡了。

examples.en: Designers often draw on nostalgia when they revive old logos and typefaces.
examples.cn: 设计师复活旧标志和旧字体时，常常借助怀旧风潮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「弄死他旧日」——把旧日翻出来反复看，人就被那份怀念缠住了；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 希腊语 nostos（归乡，与「奥德赛」的归乡主题相关）+ algos（痛苦）→ 近代拉丁语 nostalgia（一六八八年由医生霍费尔新造，指士兵的思乡病）→ 法语 nostalgie → 英语 nostalgia，核心义「归乡之痛」，后引申为「对逝去时光的怀念」。

sensesIntro.en: Nostalgia begins as the bodily pain of a soldier far from home, then spreads to any lost time, to a polished picture of the past, and finally to the styles and goods that sell that picture.
sensesIntro.cn: nostalgia 起初指远离家乡的士兵身上那种近乎身体的痛，随后扩展到任何逝去的时光，再扩展到被美化了的过去图景，最后指贩卖这幅图景的风格与商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soldier far from home holds an old photograph and gazes down the road that leads back.
core.cn: 核心意象：远离家乡的士兵握着旧照片，望向那条通往家的路。

branches.en: THE MEMORY: longing for any period of one life, felt as pleasure plus loss.
branches.cn: 记忆线：对人生中任何一段时光的怀念，混合着愉悦与失落。

branches.en: THE HOME: the oldest sense, longing for a place one has left, still current in medical and migrant writing.
branches.cn: 家乡线：最古老的义项，思念自己离开的地方，在医学与移民写作中仍然常见。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: memory polishes the past, so longing hardens into the claim that it was better.
branches.cn: 镜子线：记忆把过去擦得发亮，怀念于是固化为「从前更好」的判断。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a shared longing is packaged as fashion, music and goods.
branches.cn: 市场线：共同的怀念被打包成时尚、音乐和商品。

branches.en: Both branches keep the built-in sting: the word is pain even when it names a home.
branches.cn: 两条支线都保留着与生俱来的刺痛：即使指向家乡，这个词里也含着痛。

intro.en: Nostalgia is a learned coinage rather than an inherited word, so its parts are Greek and its English family is built with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: nostalgia 是学术性的新造词，而不是从古语言自然传下来的词，因此它的构件来自希腊语，英语词族则用普通后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek nostos and algos; the whole word was first written in modern Latin by a physician in 1688.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的构件是希腊语 nostos 与 algos；整个词最早于一六八八年由一位医生用近代拉丁语写出。

items.example: Nostos supplies the homecoming half of the image.
items.exampleCN: nostos 提供意象中「归乡」的那一半。

items.example: Algos supplies the ache that makes the word bittersweet.
items.exampleCN: algos 提供让这个词苦甜交织的那份痛。

items.meaning: pain in a part of the body
items.example: The ending -algia appears in many medical terms.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -algia 出现在许多医学词中。

items.meaning: longing for the past or for home
items.example: Nostalgia keeps both the home and the pain.
items.exampleCN: nostalgia 同时保留了「家」与「痛」。

items.meaning: relating to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ic forms nostalgic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 nostalgic。

items.example: Nostalgic describes the person or the object.
items.exampleCN: nostalgic 既可以形容人，也可以形容事物。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms nostalgically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ally 构成 nostalgically。

items.meaning: a person who does or favours something
items.meaningCN: 做某事或偏好某事的人
items.example: The suffix -ist forms nostalgist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 nostalgist。

items.meaning: a person who is fond of nostalgia
items.example: Nostalgist is a rare but recorded word.
items.exampleCN: nostalgist 是罕用但有记录的词。

definition_zh: 怀旧的；思乡的；引起怀旧情绪的；恋旧的
definition_en: feeling happy and slightly sad when you think about the past, or making people feel that way
core_image: 老人摸着旧留声机，耳边响起年轻时的曲子，嘴角带笑，眼睛却发亮
scene: 深夜的老街空了，商店橱窗里摆着一台旧收音机，还在放几十年前的歌。The sight of the old radio made him nostalgic for the summers of his childhood.
sceneCN: 这里 nostalgic 是「怀旧的」（第 1 个义项：对往昔感到又暖又酸的怀念）；句意：看见那台旧收音机，让他怀念起童年的夏天。

pos.zh: 形容词：怀旧的；思乡的；令人怀旧的

derivatives.zh: nostalgic 去掉后缀 -ic，构成名词，怀旧；怀乡之情
nostalgic 加后缀 -ally 构成，怀着怀旧之情地
与 nostalgic 同源的名词，nostalgia 加 -ist 构成，怀旧者

senses.title: Feeling fond and sad about the past
senses.definition: feeling a warm but bittersweet longing when you remember the past
senses.definitionCN: 回想起过去时产生的、既温暖又略带酸楚的怀念
senses.example: She grew nostalgic about her student days when the old song came on.
senses.exampleCN: 旧歌响起时，她对学生时代变得格外怀念。
senses.why: The adjective simply describes a person filled with the noun: the longing of nostalgia has found someone to live in.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是在描述被这个名词充满的人：nostalgia 的怀念之情找到了一个具体的人来寄托。

senses.title: Missing home
senses.definition: longing for home and the familiar places one has left
senses.definitionCN: 思念家乡和那些已离开的熟悉地方
senses.example: He felt nostalgic for home during his first winter abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外度过的第一个冬天，他很想家。
senses.why: Because the noun began as homesickness, the adjective still covers the literal longing for home, not only for vanished times.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词最初就是「思乡病」，所以形容词也仍然保留着对家乡的字面思念，不只指对逝去时光的怀念。

senses.title: Causing nostalgia in others
senses.titleCN: 令人怀旧的；带有怀旧色彩的
senses.definition: describing things, styles or places that recall an earlier era and stir memories
senses.definitionCN: 形容事物、风格或地点让人想起更早的年代，勾起回忆
senses.example: The café has a nostalgic design, with old wooden tables and hand-written menus.
senses.exampleCN: 这间咖啡馆是怀旧风格，摆着旧木桌，挂着的手写菜单也是。
senses.why: The feeling can be shifted from the person to the object that triggers it, so a shop, a song or a photograph can itself be nostalgic.
senses.whyCN: 这种情感可以从人身上移到触发它的事物上，因此一家店、一首歌或一张照片本身也可以称作 nostalgic。

intro.en: Nostalgic was coined in English in the eighteenth century as the adjective of the medical noun nostalgia.
intro.cn: nostalgic 是十八世纪英语新造的形容词，由医学术语名词 nostalgia 加后缀 -ic 构成。

items.en: Greek nostos, homecoming, and algos, pain, are the two parts that late medicine put together.
items.cn: 希腊语 nostos（归乡）与 algos（痛苦）是近代医学组合起来的两个构件。

items.en: The Swiss physician Johannes Hofer coined the Latin noun nostalgia for the homesickness of soldiers.
items.cn: 瑞士医生约翰内斯·霍费尔造出拉丁语名词 nostalgia，指士兵的思乡病。

items.en: English took both the noun and an adjective ending in -ic; early uses stay close to the medical setting.
items.cn: 英语把名词和以 -ic 结尾的形容词一并借入；早期用法仍紧贴医学语境。

items.en: As the illness reading faded, nostalgic spread to ordinary letters and diaries about home and childhood.
items.cn: 随着「病症」的解释消退，nostalgic 扩散到普通人的书信和日记中，用来讲家乡和童年。

items.en: The object of the feeling broadened, so nostalgic can describe either a person or the song, room or town that sets the feeling off.
items.cn: 这种情感的对象变宽了，于是 nostalgic 既可形容人，也可形容引发它的歌、房间或小镇。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the word family and two near spellings that belong elsewhere; the near-meaning group holds other ways of looking backwards.
note.cn: 形近组收这一词族的成员，以及两个拼写相近但另有出处的词；近义组收其他回望过去的说法。

entries.definition: the noun for the bittersweet longing that the adjective describes
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「怀旧、怀乡之情」，是本词直接脱落 -ic 得到的词基。

entries.definition: adverb: in a nostalgic manner
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「怀着怀旧之情地」，由本词加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: a drug that relieves pain; only the Greek element algos is shared
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「止痛药、止痛的」，只共用表示「痛苦」的希腊成分 algos，整词词源不同。

entries.definition: moved by tender feelings, especially ones that are easily dismissed as excessive
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多愁善感的、感伤的」，情感色彩更软，也更容易被看成过头。

entries.definition: full of quiet, slightly sad longing, often for something that cannot come back
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怅惘的、盼望而不可得的」，带文学色彩，偏安静的哀思。

entries.definition: missing home while away; plain and everyday where nostalgic is a little more literary
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「想家的」，日常而朴素；nostalgic 则稍带书面与文学色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the adjective to the noun behind it and to the prepositions it really takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子把形容词与其背后的名词连起来，并记住它实际搭配的介词。

normal.en: Drop -ic from nostalgic and you get nostalgia, the noun it describes.
normal.cn: 把 nostalgic 末尾的 -ic 去掉，就得到它对应的名词 nostalgia。

normal.en: The usual prepositions are about and for: nostalgic about the past, nostalgic for home.
normal.cn: 常用介词是 about 和 for：nostalgic about the past 与 nostalgic for home。

normal.en: The old Greek pieces are nostos, homecoming, and algos, pain: nostalgic keeps both.
normal.cn: 古老的希腊构件是 nostos（归乡）与 algos（痛苦）：nostalgic 把两者都留着。

normal.en: Since it describes a state rather than a quality, the comparison is more nostalgic.
normal.cn: 因为它描述一种状态而不是固定属性，比较级要写 more nostalgic。

normal.en: Compare the pair: a nostalgic person feels it, a nostalgic café causes it.
normal.cn: 对比这一对：nostalgic 的人感受到它，nostalgic 的咖啡馆则制造它。

abstract.en: Picture a hand touching a warm, scratched record: the warmth says the memory is kind, the scratches say it is already past.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抚过一张温热而有划痕的唱片：温热说明记忆是好的，划痕说明它已经过去了。

abstract.en: Imagine a compass needle that no longer points north but points back toward a house you left.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚不再指向北方、而是指向你离开的那座房子的指南针。

abstract.en: Think of an old shop that sells nothing but a tone: one lamp, one chair, one clock all tuned to an earlier decade.
abstract.cn: 想象一家只卖一种氛围的旧店：一盏灯、一把椅子、一架钟，全都调到从前的年代。

examples.en: Grandpa became nostalgic when he heard the song from his wedding day.
examples.cn: 爷爷听到婚礼那天的歌，变得非常怀念。

examples.en: The film is nostalgic without being sentimental about the past.
examples.cn: 这部电影带着怀旧色彩，却没有对过去滥情。

examples.en: Students living abroad often feel nostalgic for the food at home.
examples.cn: 在国外的学生常常想念家里的饭菜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「挪死他们」——搬家搬得太远，回不了旧屋，只能对着旧物发愣，这便生出怀念；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 希腊语 nostos（归乡）+ algos（痛苦）→ 近代拉丁语 nostalgia（一六八八年，思乡病）→ 英语形容词 nostalgic（加后缀 -ic）→ 名词 nostalgia 与副词 nostalgically 各自展开，核心义「归乡之痛」引申为「怀旧的」。

sensesIntro.en: Nostalgic keeps the structure of its noun: it first names the person who feels the ache, then the person who misses home, and finally the thing that produces the ache.
sensesIntro.cn: nostalgic 保留了名词的结构：先指感受到这份隐痛的人，再指想家的人，最后指制造这份隐痛的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man touches an old gramophone, and a tune from his youth turns his eyes bright.
core.cn: 核心意象：老人摸着旧留声机，年轻时的曲子让他的眼睛发亮。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the adjective lives in the one who remembers, mixing warmth with loss.
branches.cn: 人的线：形容词落在记得过去的人身上，温暖与失落并存。

branches.en: THE HOME: the literal missing of home survives from the medical origin of the noun.
branches.cn: 家乡线：对家乡的字面思念从名词的医学出身一直保留下来。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: songs, rooms and towns become nostalgic because they carry the trigger.
branches.cn: 事物线：歌、房间与小镇因为带有触发点，也被称作 nostalgic。

branches.en: The feeling and the object that sets it off are two ends of the same memory.
branches.cn: 情感与其触发物是同一段记忆的两端。

branches.en: The same word covers the plain longing for home and the polished image of it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既覆盖朴素的思乡，也覆盖被修饰过的家乡形象。

intro.en: Nostalgic is a straightforward English adjective on a learned noun; only the -ic ending is added by English.
intro.cn: nostalgic 是加在学术名词上的直接形容词，英语只额外添了 -ic 这一词尾。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek nostos and algos, joined into a modern Latin medical noun in 1688.
latinIntro.cn: 构件是希腊语 nostos 与 algos，一六八八年被合成近代拉丁语的医学名词。

items.example: Nostos is the homecoming part of the image.
items.exampleCN: nostos 是意象中「归乡」的那一半。

items.example: Algos gives the word its hidden hurt.
items.exampleCN: algos 给这个词带来隐藏的痛感。

items.meaning: longing for home or the past
items.example: The noun is the base that nostalgic describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词就是形容词 nostalgic 所描述的那种状态。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns nostalgia into nostalgic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把 nostalgia 变成 nostalgic。

items.example: Nostalgic covers both feeling and trigger.
items.exampleCN: nostalgic 既指感受，也指触发物。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms nostalgically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ally 构成 nostalgically。

items.example: Nostalgically marks how an action is done.
items.exampleCN: nostalgically 说明动作是以何种心情完成的。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms nostalgist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 nostalgist。

items.example: Nostalgist is the rare noun for the lover of old times.
items.exampleCN: nostalgist 是表示「爱恋旧时光者」的罕用名词。
