definition_zh: 值得注意的；显著的；出众的；名人
definition_en: important, interesting or special enough to attract attention, or a person well known for something
core_image: 一排普通的书中间立着一本烫金书脊的厚书，一眼就能看见
scene: 公司楼下的咖啡角最近变了样，墙上挂满了员工手绘的小画。One sketch was hung a little higher than the rest, which is why it was the notable piece in that corner.
sceneCN: 这里 notable 是「值得注意的、显著的」（第 1 个义项：显眼到引人关注）；句意：有一幅速写挂得比别的都高一点，所以它成了那个角落里最引人注目的一件作品。

pos.zh: 形容词：值得注意的；显著的；出众的

derivatives.zh: notable 加后缀 -ly 构成，尤其；显著地
notable 加后缀 -ity 构成，显著；著名；知名人士
与本词同源的基础词，注意；留意
同源于拉丁语 notus，因坏事而出名；声名狼藉

senses.title: Worthy of attention because it stands out
senses.definition: important or interesting enough to deserve attention
senses.definitionCN: 重要或有趣到值得人们关注
senses.example: The most notable difference is the colour of the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 最显著的差别是屋瓦的颜色。
senses.why: Latin notabilis comes from notare, to mark, so a notable thing is one that has been marked, noticed and set apart from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notabilis 来自 notare（做标记），所以 notable 的事物是被做了记号、被注意并从中挑出来的那一个。

senses.title: Famous or distinguished for something
senses.definition: well known or admired for a skill, achievement or quality
senses.definitionCN: 因某种技能、成就或品质而广为人知或受人敬佩
senses.example: She is notable for her patience with young learners.
senses.exampleCN: 她以待年幼学生的耐心而闻名。
senses.why: Once the mark of attention is set, it can become reputation: the notable person is the one everyone has marked down in memory, always in a good way.
senses.whyCN: 注目的记号一旦固定下来，就会变成名声：notable 的人是那个被所有人记在心里的那个，而且总是往好的一面记。

senses.title: Remarkable in a striking or unusual way
senses.titleCN: 引人注目的；不同寻常的
senses.definition: unusual enough to be surprising, sometimes without being especially admired
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常到令人惊讶，有时并不含特别赞赏之意
senses.example: It is notable that none of the witnesses mentioned the second car.
senses.exampleCN: 值得注意的是，没有一位证人提到那第二辆车。
senses.why: Marking does not say whether a thing is good or bad, so notable can simply flag a striking fact, as when a report says it is notable that something did not happen.
senses.whyCN: 「做记号」并不说明事物好坏，因此 notable 也可以只是标出一个显眼的事实，比如报告里说「值得注意的是某事没有发生」。

senses.title: A well-known person
senses.definition: a person who is well known in a place or circle, especially when seen as a group
senses.definitionCN: 在某地或某圈子里很有名的人，常用于指一群人
senses.example: The reception brought together local notables from business and politics.
senses.exampleCN: 这场招待会聚集了本地政商两界的知名人士。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun: the marked people, called notables, are exactly the ones who fill a front row at a celebration.
senses.whyCN: 形容词名词化：被「做上记号」的人被称作 notables，正是庆典上坐在前排的那批人。

intro.en: Notable comes from Latin notabilis, worthy of notice, built on notare, to mark, from nota, a mark.
intro.cn: notable 来自拉丁语 notabilis（值得注意的），词基是 notare（做标记），再往前是 nota（记号）。

items.en: Latin nota meant a mark, a sign or a written note, and notare meant to mark or take note of.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为「记号、标志、书面记录」，notare 意为「标记、留意」。

items.en: The adjective notabilis meant remarkable or famous, literally that which can or should be marked.
items.cn: 形容词 notabilis 意为「显著的、著名的」，字面就是「可以或应该被标记的」。

items.en: Old French took notabilis over as notable, and manuscripts of the thirteenth century already record the English form.
items.cn: 古法语把 notabilis 借作 notable，十三世纪的手稿里已经能见到英语形式。

items.en: In early English the word was also used as a noun meaning a notable person, a use that has come back into fashion.
items.cn: 早期英语中这个词也作名词，指有名的人；这一用法后来一度沉寂，如今又流行起来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective for facts and features, and uses the plural notables for a gathering of people who are locally famous.
items.cn: 现代英语用形容词去修饰事实和特征，用复数 notables 指一批在本地有名的人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds close spellings and members of the note family; the near-meaning group holds other words for standing out.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词和 note 词族的成员；近义组收其他表示「突出、有名」的词。

entries.definition: adverb: especially, or in a way that is easy to notice
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「尤其、显著地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: to write something down in a system of signs, such as music notation
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用符号记录、记谱」，与 notable 同源于「标记」的动词。

entries.definition: a system of written signs, for example in music or mathematics
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记谱法、符号系统」，同源于拉丁语 nota（记号）。

entries.definition: unusual and worth talking about, often with surprise or admiration
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非凡的、引人注目的」，常带惊讶或赞叹，力度通常比 notable 更强。

entries.definition: important and easily seen in a place, group or field
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「显要的、突出的」，强调在群体或领域中的地位与可见度。

entries.definition: widely known and respected, usually for good work
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「享有盛名的」，强调名声广且受到尊敬，范围常超出本地。

entries.definition: easy to see or feel, without any claim of importance
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显可察的」，只说明容易察觉，不含「重要」的判断。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real Latin root and on the phrases that actually follow the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子建立在这个词真实的拉丁词根上，并记住它常跟的搭配。

normal.en: Note and notable share one root: what you note is what becomes notable.
normal.cn: note 与 notable 同一个根：你留意到的东西，才会成为值得注意的东西。

normal.en: A notable exception is the phrase a report uses when one case refuses to follow the rule.
normal.cn: a notable exception 是报告里用的说法，指某个不守规律的特例。

normal.en: Most notable for is the usual way to say what a thing is best known for.
normal.cn: most notable for 是说明某物「最出名之处」的常用说法。

normal.en: The adverb notably marks the strongest item in a list: notably three of the twelve.
normal.cn: 副词 notably 用来标出清单里最突出的一项：notably three of the twelve。

normal.en: Compare notable and noticed: noticed is passive, notable is a standing reputation.
normal.cn: 对比 notable 与 noticed：noticed 只是一时被看见，notable 则是长期立得住的名声。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf where one spine has a strip of gold leaf: the shelf did not change, one book was marked.
abstract.cn: 想象一排书里有一本烫了金边的书脊：书架没变，只是有一本被做了记号。

abstract.en: Imagine a map dotted with small pins: the pins are the notables, the towns everyone writes down.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上插着许多小图钉：那些图钉就是有名的人和事，人人都要记下来的那些。

abstract.en: Think of a finger lifted in a meeting whenever one fact deserves a pause: that lifted finger is the word notable.
abstract.cn: 想象开会时有人为一件事抬起手指示意「注意这里」：那根抬起的手指就是 notable。

examples.en: The region is notable for its dry summers and mild winters.
examples.cn: 该地区以夏季干燥、冬季温和而著称。

examples.en: There are a few notable exceptions to the new timetable.
examples.cn: 新时刻表有几个值得注意的例外。

examples.en: Local notables were invited to speak at the opening ceremony.
examples.cn: 当地知名人士受邀在开幕式上发言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「挪特簿」——一位名人被挪到了特别登记簿的最上面，人人一翻就看见；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 nota（记号、记录）→ notare（做标记、留意）→ notabilis（值得标记的）→ 古法语 notable → 英语 notable，核心义「被做上记号、值得留意」，引申为「显著的」「出名的」与名词「名人」。同根还有 note、notice、notion 与 notoriety。

sensesIntro.en: Notable runs from a fact worth a mark, to a person worth a reputation, to an oddity worth a raised eyebrow, and finally to the people who carry the reputation as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: notable 从值得记一笔的事实，走到值得扬名的人，再走到值得挑眉细看的不寻常之处，最后落到以名词身份承载名声的那批人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: among plain books, one spine is marked with a strip of gold, so the eye finds it at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一排普通书籍中间，有一本书脊被烫了金边，眼睛一下就能找到它。

branches.en: THE MARK: a fact or feature is set apart from the rest and so deserves attention.
branches.cn: 标记线：某个事实或特征被从中挑出，因此值得关注。

branches.en: THE NAME: repeated marking settles into a fine reputation, and the word means known for something.
branches.cn: 名声线：反复被标记沉淀为好评，这个词便表示「因某事闻名」。

branches.en: THE FLAG: marking says nothing about value, so notable can point at a surprising fact.
branches.cn: 提示线：标记并不评判好坏，因此 notable 也可以只是点出一个令人意外的事实。

branches.en: THE ROW: the adjective becomes a noun, naming the well-known people who sit in it.
branches.cn: 前排线：形容词名词化，用来指坐在前排的那些知名人士。

branches.en: Both the ordinary remark and the raised eyebrow keep the plain sense of being noticed.
branches.cn: 无论平常提及还是特意惊讶，两者都保留着「被注意到」这层本义。

intro.en: Notable is built on the Latin marking root, and English adds -ly and -ity to make its family.
intro.cn: notable 建立在拉丁语「标记」词根上，英语再加 -ly 与 -ity 扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin nota, notare and notabilis are all recorded; the deeper Indo-European origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nota、notare 与 notabilis 都有文献记录；更早的印欧语来源不确定。

items.example: Nota is the mark that the whole family shares.
items.exampleCN: nota 是整个词族共用的「记号」。

items.example: Notare turns the mark into an action.
items.exampleCN: notare 把「记号」变成动作。

items.meaning: able to be, worthy of being
items.example: The suffix -abilis makes notabilis worth marking.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -abilis 使 notabilis 意为「值得被标记」。

items.example: Notabilis is the direct source of notable.
items.exampleCN: notabilis 是 notable 的直接来源。

items.example: Note is the simple English base of the family.
items.exampleCN: note 是这一词族最简单的英语基础词。

items.example: Notable keeps the mark as a standing quality.
items.exampleCN: notable 把「记号」保留为一种常态品质。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms notably.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 notably。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms notability.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 notability。

items.example: Notoriety is the darker cousin of notability.
items.exampleCN: notoriety 是 notability 更阴暗的表亲。

definition_zh: 符号；记号；记谱法；记号表示法
definition_en: a system of symbols used to represent numbers, music, science or other information
core_image: 一张纸上用简短的符号把复杂的旋律或数量记录下来
scene: 乐手翻开谱子，先读懂所唱音符的记号，再开口。The singer read the musical notation on the page before opening her mouth.
sceneCN: 这里 notation 是「符号、记号体系」（第 1 个义项：用符号记录信息的一套方式）；句意：这位歌手在开口前先读了纸上的乐谱记号。

derivatives.zh: 由 notare 加英文后缀 -e 构成的名词，义为「笔记；音符；记号」
notation 加形容词后缀 -al，义为「记号的；记谱法的」
由拉丁 notare 加英文动词后缀 -ate，义为「用符号记录；（为音乐）记谱」
前缀 an-（来自 ad-，向）+ notare，义为「给……加批注」
annotate 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「批注；注解」

senses.title: A system of written symbols
senses.definition: a set of written signs or symbols used to stand for sounds, numbers or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 一套用来代表声音、数字或思想的书写符号
senses.example: Each culture invented its own notation for counting.
senses.exampleCN: 每种文化都发明了自己计数的记号体系。
senses.why: The Latin verb notare means to mark, so notation is literally the act of marking things down.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 notare 意为「做记号」，因此 notation 字面上就是「把东西标记下来」的行为，符号体系由标记自然延伸而来。

senses.title: Musical notation
senses.definition: the written system of notes, staves and marks that tells musicians how to play a piece
senses.definitionCN: 用音符、谱线与各种标记告诉乐手如何演奏一部作品的书写体系
senses.example: The choir learned the piece by ear rather than from notation.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团是凭耳朵学会这首曲子的，而不是看乐谱。
senses.why: Music was one of the earliest fields to turn sound into written marks, so the general marking system found its clearest home here.
senses.whyCN: 音乐是最早把声音变成书面标记的领域之一，于是这种通用的标记方式在这里找到了最典型的用法。

senses.title: Scientific notation
senses.definition: a way of writing very large or very small numbers as a figure between one and ten multiplied by a power of ten
senses.definitionCN: 把极大或极小的数写成一到十之间的数乘以十的若干次方的方法
senses.example: Astronomers write huge distances in scientific notation.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家用科学记数法书写巨大的距离。
senses.why: When numbers grow too long to handle, the marking system compresses them into a short, standard symbol.
senses.whyCN: 当数字长得难以操作时，这套标记方式就把它们压缩成简短而标准的符号。

senses.title: A single sign or mark
senses.definition: one particular written mark used in a document, diagram or set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 某份文件、图表或规则中使用的某一个具体书写标记
senses.example: The editor flagged the unclear notation in the margin.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在页边标出了那个不清楚的记号。
senses.why: From the whole system, the word readily narrows to any single mark produced by that system.
senses.whyCN: 从整套体系出发，这个词很自然地缩小到该体系产生的任何一个单独标记。

senses.title: The act or process of marking
senses.definition: the process of recording information with symbols rather than in ordinary words
senses.definitionCN: 用符号而不是普通文字来记录信息的过程
senses.example: Dance steps were once passed on without any notation at all.
senses.exampleCN: 舞蹈步法曾经完全不靠任何符号记录，只靠口头相传。
senses.why: The Latin suffix -tion names an action, so notation can mean the very act of putting something into symbols.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁后缀 -tion 表示行为，所以 notation 也可以指「把某物变成符号」这个动作本身。

intro.en: Notation comes from Latin notatio, a marking or a note, from nota, a mark, with the verb notare, to mark.
intro.cn: notation 来自拉丁语 notatio（标记、记号），源于 nota（标记）与动词 notare（做记号）。

items.en: Nota means a mark, a sign or a known sign, with notare meaning to mark.
items.cn: nota 意为标记、符号；notare 意为做记号。

items.en: Notatio means a marking or a written note.
items.cn: notatio 意为标记或写下的记录。

items.en: Notation is used for a written note or memoranda.
items.cn: notation 在法语中用于指书面记录或笔记。

items.en: The word enters English meaning a note or a marked sign.
items.cn: 该词以「笔记、标记符号」之义进入英语。

items.en: Music and mathematics give it the standard sense of a system of written symbols.
items.cn: 音乐与数学赋予它「成套书写符号体系」的标准含义。

items.en: Scientific writing extends the word to computer and scientific mark systems.
items.cn: 现代科技写作又把该词延伸到计算机与科学记数等符号系统。

note.en: Notation is the noun of marking, closely tied to note, annotate and the Latin verb notare.
note.cn: notation 是表示「做标记」的名词，与 note、annotate 以及拉丁动词 notare 关系紧密。

entries.definition: a short written record or a single musical sound
entries.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录；单个乐音

entries.definition: based on an idea rather than on fact
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：它来自「观念」一词，与记号无关

entries.definition: a note added to explain a text
entries.definitionCN: 为解释文本而加上的批注

entries.definition: a sign that stands for something else
a fast system of writing using quick signs
a system of writing used by a language
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言所用的书写体系

normalIntro.en: Notation is things marked down: a compact set of signs that carries a whole song or number.
normalIntro.cn: notation 就是被标记下来的东西：一小套符号承载整首曲子或整个数量。

normal.en: Link it to note: a note is one mark, notation is the whole family of marks.
normal.cn: 联系 note：note 是一个记号，notation 是整个记号体系。

normal.en: Musical notation is music turned into written signs.
normal.cn: musical notation 就是把音乐变成书面符号。

normal.en: The suffix -tion is a Latin action suffix, so notation can mean the act of marking.
normal.cn: 后缀 -tion 是拉丁语动作后缀，所以 notation 也能表示「做记号」这一行为。

normal.en: Annotate means to add notes, and annotation means the notes added.
normal.cn: annotate 表示添加注解，annotation 表示所加的注解。

normal.en: Compare notice and notify: they share the same root of knowing, not the marking root of notation.
normal.cn: 对比 notice 与 notify：它们同出「知道」的词根，而不是 notation 的「标记」词根，只是长得像。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of symbols so compact that a whole song fits on one page.
abstract.cn: 想象一页符号密密麻麻，整首歌都被装进一张纸里。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher tapping with chalk and writing tiny marks above each phrase of music.
abstract.cn: 想象老师用粉笔敲黑板，在每段旋律上方写下小小的记号。

abstract.en: Think of a long number with many zeros collapsing into a short power of ten.
abstract.cn: 想象一串长长的带很多零的数字缩成一个短短的十的幂。

examples.en: Scientific notation keeps long numbers short and tidy.
examples.cn: 科学记数法让冗长的数字变得简短整洁。

examples.en: The old manuscript uses a notation that few scholars can read.
examples.cn: 这份古老手稿使用的记号体系，如今只有少数学者能读懂。

examples.en: Students were taught to read musical notations before they sang.
examples.cn: 学生们在唱歌之前先被教会了识读乐谱记号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特申」——诺（not）字头上加个记号，就记成了「记号体系」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 nota（标记、记号）+ notare（做记号）→ notatio（标记）→ 法语 notation → 英语 notation，核心义「把事物标记下来」。

sensesIntro.en: Notation begins as a general system of marks, then branches into music, science, single marks and the act of marking.
sensesIntro.cn: notation 起初泛指一套标记体系，随后分化为乐谱、科学记数、单个记号与「做记号」这一行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page where short marks store a whole song.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页纸上用简短记号装下整首歌。

branches.en: The general system of written symbols is the base sense.
branches.cn: 成套书写符号体系是基础义项。

branches.en: Music is the most famous use of a marking system.
branches.cn: 音乐是标记体系最著名的应用。

branches.en: Science compresses long numbers into short standard marks.
branches.cn: 科学把冗长数字压缩成简短的标准化记号。

branches.en: A whole system and any single mark inside it share one image.
branches.cn: 整套体系与体系中任何一个单独记号共享同一个意象。

branches.en: The mark itself and the act of marking are two sides of one word.
branches.cn: 记号本身与做记号的动作是同一个词的两面。

intro.en: Notation is built from the Latin root nota with the action suffix -tion, and English forms a family with note, notate, annotate and annotation.
intro.cn: notation 由拉丁词根 nota 加上动作后缀 -tion 构成，英语围绕它形成 note、notate、annotate 与 annotation 等词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin nota means a mark, and notare means to mark, so the family always points to writing signs down.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为标记，notare 意为做记号，所以这个词族始终指向「把符号写下来」。

items.example: Nota gives the marking image at the centre.
items.exampleCN: nota 提供了位于中心的「标记」意象。

items.example: Notare is the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: notare 是这个名词背后的动作。

items.example: Notatio is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: notatio 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.example: The suffix -tion turns the verb into a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 把动词变成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Notation keeps the noun sense of markings.
items.exampleCN: notation 保留了「标记」的名词含义。

items.meaning: a short written record or a musical sound
items.example: Note is the plain everyday member of the family.
items.exampleCN: note 是这个词族里最日常的一员。

items.example: Notate is the verb built directly on the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: notate 是直接建立在拉丁词根上的动词。

items.meaning: relating to a system of marks
items.example: Notational describes anything that belongs to marks.
items.exampleCN: notational 描述属于记号体系的东西。

items.meaning: to add notes to a text
items.example: Annotate adds the prefix meaning towards.
items.exampleCN: annotate 加上了表示「朝向」的前缀。

items.example: Annotation is the note added to a page.
items.exampleCN: annotation 是加在页面上的注解。

definition_zh: 值得注意的；重要的；显著的
definition_en: important or interesting enough to be noticed and remembered
core_image: 灯下一页笔记被翻开，旁边的人忍不住停下来看一眼
scene: 评委们听完所有演奏，只对练琴少年的控制力点头称赞。After hearing every player, the judges agreed that the young pianist showed noteworthy control.
sceneCN: 这里 noteworthy 是「值得注意的」（第 1 个义项：重要或有趣到值得关注）；句意：听完所有演奏后，评委们一致认为这位少年钢琴家表现出的控制力值得注意。

pos.zh: 值得注意的；重要的；显著的

derivatives.zh: 词的第一部分，加 -worthy 之前表示「注意到；记下」，由「记住」引申为「值得被记住」
noteworthy 加名词后缀 -ness，义为「值得注意之处；重要性」
worthy 加名词后缀 -ness，义为「价值；值得的程度」
note 加过去分词词尾 -ed，义为「著名的；知名的」

senses.title: Deserving attention
senses.titleCN: 值得注意的；值得关注的
senses.definition: important or unusual enough that people stop and take notice
senses.definitionCN: 重要或特别到让人们停下来关注的程度
senses.example: Her calm handling of the crisis was noteworthy.
senses.exampleCN: 她应对危机时的镇定值得关注。
senses.why: The word is literally note plus worthy: what is observed and written down is worth being noticed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是 note 加 worthy，即「值得被注意、被记下」，所以指值得关注之事。

senses.title: Important or significant
senses.definition: large or serious enough to matter in a real way
senses.definitionCN: 规模或分量足够大、足以产生真实影响
senses.example: A noteworthy gain of jobs followed the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 新方案之后出现了显著的就业岗位增长。
senses.why: Once something is worth noticing, it usually carries real weight, so the word slides into meaning significant.
senses.whyCN: 一件事一旦值得注意，往往确实有分量，于是这个词自然滑向「重要、显著」的意思。

senses.title: Unusually good or impressive
senses.definition: good or striking in a way that earns approval
senses.definitionCN: 因出色或亮眼而赢得他人赞许
senses.example: The choir gave a noteworthy performance in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团在雨中献上了一场出色的演出。
senses.why: The worthy half carries a sense of merit, so anything noteworthy is also something worth praising.
senses.whyCN: worthy 那一半带有「有价值、有优点」的意味，所以值得注意之事常常同时值得称赞。

senses.title: Worth recording or remembering
senses.definition: remarkable enough to be written down or kept in memory
senses.definitionCN: 特别到值得被写下或牢牢记住
senses.example: Two noteworthy events marked that autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 那个秋天发生了两件值得记录的大事。
senses.why: The note half is about writing something down, so what deserves noting also deserves remembering.
senses.whyCN: note 那一半关于「写下来」，所以值得记下的事，自然也值得被记住。

senses.title: Shown in a mild, formal way
senses.titleCN: 低调而正式地表示“值得留意的”
senses.definition: used in formal writing to point something out politely without strong praise
senses.definitionCN: 在正式书面语中礼貌指出某事、却不作强烈赞扬的用法
senses.example: It is noteworthy that no one objected at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 值得注意的是，会上没有人提出反对。
senses.why: Formal reports prefer this understated twin of worthy of attention, keeping praise controlled.
senses.whyCN: 正式报告偏爱这个低调的说法来代替「值得关注」，让褒扬保持克制。

intro.en: Noteworthy is an English compound of note and worthy, put together in the sixteenth century to mean deserving notice.
intro.cn: noteworthy 是英语复合词，由 note 与 worthy 组合而成，一般认为形成于十六世纪，意为「值得注意」。

items.en: The verb note comes from Latin notare, to mark or write, through Old French noter.
items.cn: 动词 note 经古法语 noter 来自拉丁语 notare（做记号、书写）。

items.en: The suffix -woerthie meant worth, and English forms -worthy in compounds.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -woerthie 表示「值得」，英语由此形成 -worthy 这一构词成分。

items.en: The compound noteworthy appears, meaning worth taking note of.
items.cn: noteworthy 作为复合词出现，意为「值得记下的」。

items.en: The word widens from worth noting to important or remarkable.
items.cn: 词义从「值得记下」扩展到「重要、不寻常」。

items.en: It survives mainly in formal prose and reports as a calm praise word.
items.cn: 现代英语中它主要用于正式散文与报告，是一种克制的褒义词。

note.en: Noteworthy pairs note, meaning to notice and write down, with worthy, meaning deserving, so the word asks whether a thing deserves attention.
note.cn: noteworthy 把「注意、记下」的 note 与「值得」的 worthy 组合起来，问的是一件事是否值得关注。

entries.definition: deserving to be noticed; famous
well known for a quality
easy to see or hear
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源走的是「通告」一路，义为「明显的」

entries.definition: unusual in a way that surprises
large or important enough to matter
so noticeable that it draws the eye

normalIntro.en: Noteworthy is a small judgement inside one word: something is worth your note.
normalIntro.cn: noteworthy 是一个词里的判断：某件事值得你记上一笔。

normal.en: Split it as note and worthy, worth your note means worth noticing.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 note 和 worthy，「值得你记一笔」就是值得注意。

normal.en: Compare notable and noteworthy: both come from the same marking root.
normal.cn: 对比 notable 与 noteworthy：两者同出「标记」词根。

normal.en: A noteworthy achievement is one worth writing into the record.
normal.cn: noteworthy achievement 就是值得写进记录的成绩。

normal.en: The word is used in reports, so it sounds calmer than remarkable.
normal.cn: 这个词多用于报告，所以语气比 remarkable 更平静。

normal.en: Do not mix it with noticeable, which means easy to see, not important.
normal.cn: 别和 noticeable 混用：后者指「容易被看到」，而不是「重要」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting a pen whenever something truly deserves a note.
abstract.cn: 想象每当有真正值得记下的事，就有一只手抬起来拿起笔。

abstract.en: Imagine an award board where only a few names shine, the rest stay plain.
abstract.cn: 想象一块荣誉墙，只有少数名字发亮，其余都平淡无光。

abstract.en: Think of a conductor bowing once to the one player who stood out.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥只朝那位突出的乐手鞠了一躬。

examples.en: The museum holds a noteworthy collection of local pottery.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆藏有一批值得一提的本地陶器。

examples.en: Nothing noteworthy happened during the long train ride.
examples.cn: 漫长的火车旅途中没有发生什么值得注意的事。

examples.en: It is noteworthy how quickly the town recovered.
examples.cn: 这座小镇恢复得如此之快，这一点值得注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「note 值得」——note（笔记）加 worthy（值得），值得落笔记下的，就是「值得注意的」；这只是拆合成词的联想，不等于它的词源。

root: 英语 note（注意；记下，源自拉丁语 nota 标记、notare 记下）+ worthy（值得，古英语 -woerthie），核心义「值得被记下、被关注」。

sensesIntro.en: Noteworthy starts from worth noticing, then widens to important, then to impressive, to worth remembering, and to a calm formal use.
sensesIntro.cn: noteworthy 从「值得注意」起步，扩展为「重要」，再延伸出「出色」、「值得铭记」以及低调的正式用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note on a page that makes a reader stop.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸上一行让人停下来的笔记。

branches.en: The basic sense insists that something deserves attention.
branches.cn: 基本义项强调某事值得关注。

branches.en: Attention turns into real importance and size.
branches.cn: 「被关注」进一步化为真正的重要性与分量。

branches.en: The worthy half brings in praise and merit.
branches.cn: worthy 那一半带来称赞与优点的意味。

branches.en: Being worth a note and being worth a formal mention share the noting image.
branches.cn: 「值得记下」与「值得在正式场合一提」共享同一个「记下」意象。

branches.en: Attention, importance and praise often describe the same success.
branches.cn: 关注、重要与称赞常常指向同一份成功。

intro.en: Noteworthy is a native compound: a Latin-based verb note joins the Old English suffix -worthy.
intro.cn: noteworthy 是英语本土复合词：拉丁来源的动词 note 与古英语后缀 -worthy 相结合。

latinIntro.en: The note part goes back to Latin nota, a mark, and notare, to mark or write.
latinIntro.cn: note 这一部分可追溯到拉丁语 nota（标记）与 notare（记号、书写）。

items.example: Note is the observing half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: note 是这个复合词中「观察」的一半。

items.example: A note is the mark left by attention.
items.exampleCN: note 是注意力留下的印记。

items.example: The suffix -worthy creates trustworthy and noteworthy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -worthy 构成了 trustworthy 与 noteworthy。

items.example: Noteworthy fuses both halves into one judgement.
items.exampleCN: noteworthy 把两半合成一个判断。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms noteworthiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 noteworthiness。

items.example: Notable uses the Latin suffix -able on the same stem.
items.exampleCN: notable 在同一词干上用了拉丁后缀 -able。

items.example: Noted is the participle of note.
items.exampleCN: noted 是 note 的分词形式。

items.example: Noticeable points to being seen rather than to importance.
items.exampleCN: noticeable 强调的是「被看到」，而不是「重要」。

items.example: Worthy carries the merit half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: worthy 承担了复合词中「价值」那一半。

definition_zh: 显著地；明显地；显而易见地
definition_en: in a way that is easy to see or feel; by an amount large enough to matter
core_image: 两个物体放在一起，其中一个肉眼一看就明显不同
scene: 入夏之后，街上的树叶明显比上周更绿更密。After the warm week, the trees along the street had become noticeably greener.
sceneCN: 这里 noticeably 是「明显地、可察觉地」（第 1 个义项：变化大到肉眼或感觉能捕捉到）；句意：温暖的一周过后，街边的树明显变绿了。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「明显的；引人注意的」
notice 加过去分词词尾 -ed，义为「被注意到的」
notice 加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed，义为「未被注意到的」
与 noticeably 形近，来自 notable，义为「尤其；显著地」

senses.title: In a way that can be seen
senses.titleCN: 可察觉到地；看得出来地
senses.definition: so clearly that the change or difference can easily be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到变化或差别很容易被注意到的程度
senses.example: The room grew noticeably quieter as the lecture began.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座一开始，教室明显安静了下来。
senses.why: The adjective noticeable means able to be noticed, and -ly adds the manner of being noticed.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 noticeable 意为「能被注意到的」，后缀 -ly 表示「以……的方式」，因此副词指「以被察觉的方式」。

senses.title: By a clear amount
senses.titleCN: 明显地（用于数量或程度比较）
senses.definition: by an amount large enough to be measured or compared clearly
senses.definitionCN: 大到可以被清楚测量或比较的幅度
senses.example: Prices are noticeably higher than last year.
senses.exampleCN: 价格明显比去年高。
senses.why: The suffix -able adds the sense of a clear degree, so the adverb compares two amounts and finds a real gap.
senses.whyCN: 形容词里的 -able 带出「程度清晰」的意味，于是副词用于比较两个数量，指出确有差距。

senses.title: Obviously or evidently
senses.definition: used to say that something is obvious to anyone who looks
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明任何观察者都能看出某事是显然的
senses.example: She was noticeably touched by the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她显然被这封信打动了。
senses.why: What is easy to notice soon reads as obvious, so the word also states what any observer would see.
senses.whyCN: 容易被察觉的东西很快就被读作「显然」，于是这个词也能陈述任何人都会看到的结论。

senses.title: Losing a noted quality
senses.titleCN: （本该出色之处）未见明显表现地；显得平平地
senses.definition: used when a quality that is expected to stand out fails to show clearly
senses.definitionCN: 在本该突出的特质没有清楚表现出来时使用的说法
senses.example: The star player seemed noticeably off form.
senses.exampleCN: 那位明星球员的状态明显不在线。
senses.why: Because the word says whether something stands out, it is often used to point out quietly when it fails to do so.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在问「是否突出」，所以常被用来委婉指出某事并没能突出。

senses.title: In a striking or remarkable way
senses.definition: in a way that stands out and draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 突出、吸引目光的方式
senses.example: Her style of speaking is noticeably unusual.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说话风格明显不同寻常。
senses.why: Being worthy of notice links the word to remarkable, so it can also mark what stands out strongly.
senses.whyCN: 「值得注意」这层意思把该词与 remarkable 连起来，于是它也能标出突出之处。

intro.en: Noticeably is an English word built from note, by way of notice, noticeable and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: noticeably 是英语自身构成的词，从 note 出发，经 notice、noticeable，再加副词结尾 -ly。

items.en: Notitia means knowledge or notice, from notus, the past participle meaning known.
items.cn: 拉丁语 notitia 意为「知晓、认识」，源于意为「已知」的分词形式 notus。

items.en: Notice means a piece of information or knowledge in French and English.
items.cn: 法语与早期英语中 notice 表示一条信息或知识。

items.en: The verb notice appears and comes to mean to become aware of.
items.cn: 动词 notice 出现，逐渐表示「察觉、注意到」。

items.en: The adjective noticeable arises, meaning able to be noticed.
items.cn: 形容词 noticeable 出现，意为「能被注意到的」。

items.en: Adding -ly gives the adverb noticeably, first in print in the 1800s.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 得到副词 noticeably，最早在十九世纪的印刷品中出现。

items.en: The adverb becomes a common way to compare visible or measurable change.
items.cn: 现代英语中它成为比较可见或可测变化的常用说法。

note.en: Noticeably belongs to the notice family, which grows out of the Latin root for knowing, and its neighbours differ in how strongly they claim that a difference is visible.
note.cn: noticeably 属于 notice 词族，源自表示「知晓」的拉丁词根，它的近邻词的差别在于多强烈地宣称某种差异看得见。

entries.definition: easy to see
to become aware of
especially, in a way worth noting
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，来自 notable，义为「尤其；显著地」

entries.definition: in a way anyone would see
entries.definitionCN: 显而易见地；任何人都看得出地

entries.definition: by an amount that matters
entries.definitionCN: 显著地；在数据上重要地

entries.definition: in a clear, distinctly different way

normalIntro.en: Noticeably is notice made visible from outside: anyone looking can tell that something has changed.
normalIntro.cn: noticeably 是「注意」被外化：任何人一看就能说出发生了变化。

normal.en: Build it step by step: notice, noticeable, and then add the adverb ending.
normal.cn: 一步步搭起来：notice、noticeable，再加副词结尾。

normal.en: It almost always pairs with a comparison: better, worse, higher, quieter.
normal.cn: 它几乎总跟比较级一起用：better、worse、higher、quieter。

normal.en: The adjective keeps the suffix -able, which means able to be noticed.
normal.cn: 形容词里的后缀 -able 表示「能够被注意到的」。

normal.en: Compare obviously: obviously claims that everyone already knows, noticeably claims that the change can be seen.
normal.cn: 对比 obviously：obviously 宣称人人早已知道，noticeably 则宣称变化看得见。

normal.en: Compare significantly: significantly measures size in data, noticeably reports what the eye finds.
normal.cn: 对比 significantly：significantly 在数据上衡量大小，noticeably 报告眼睛看到的变化。

abstract.en: Picture two leaves side by side and your eye jumps straight to the greener one.
abstract.cn: 想象两片叶子并排放在一起，你的眼睛直接跳到更绿的那片。

abstract.en: Imagine stepping on a scale and seeing a clear jump in the number.
abstract.cn: 想象踩上体重秤，看见数字清楚地跳了一格。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd that turns quiet the moment a speaker raises a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者一举手，人群立刻安静下来。

examples.en: The delivery arrived noticeably later than promised.
examples.cn: 快递送达的时间明显比承诺的晚。

examples.en: Since the change, the streets have become noticeably cleaner.
examples.cn: 自从那次改变之后，街道明显干净了许多。

examples.en: His voice was noticeably softer when he spoke of his mother.
examples.cn: 他提到母亲时，声音明显柔和下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「note 一色」——note 加 ise，再加 able 与 ly，一眼就能 note 到的「一色」变化，就是「明显地」；这只是拆词谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 notus（已知）+ 法语 notice（知晓、通知）→ 英语 notice（注意）→ noticeable（可注意到的）→ noticeably（以可注意到的方式），核心义「看得见、察觉得到」。

sensesIntro.en: Noticeably starts from what the eye can catch, then extends to clear amount, to obvious fact, to quiet failure to stand out, and to strong remark.
sensesIntro.cn: noticeably 从「看得见」出发，延伸到清楚的幅度、明显的事实、未能突出的含蓄说法，以及强烈的「引人注目」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things side by side, and the eye jumps to the different one.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西并排放着，眼睛直接跳到不同之处。

branches.en: The basic sense reports a visible change.
branches.cn: 基本义项报告一种看得见的变化。

branches.en: A clear amount turns noticing into comparison.
branches.cn: 清楚的幅度把「注意」变成了比较。

branches.en: What anyone sees becomes an obvious fact.
branches.cn: 人人可见之事就成了显然的事实。

branches.en: Failing to stand out and strongly standing out are two edges of the same noticing.
branches.cn: 「没突出」与「很突出」是同一个「注意」意象的两端。

branches.en: A comparable amount and an obvious fact both rest on clear evidence.
branches.cn: 可比较的幅度与显然的事实都建立在清楚的证据上。

intro.en: Noticeably stacks Latin-derived notice with the English suffixes -able and -ly.
intro.cn: noticeably 由拉丁来源的 notice 叠加英语后缀 -able 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The family goes back to Latin notus, meaning known, and notitia, meaning knowledge or notice.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族可追溯到拉丁语 notus（已知）与 notitia（知晓、通知）。

items.meaning: to see or become aware of
items.example: Notice is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: notice 是这个词族的基词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms noticeable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 noticeable。

items.example: Noticeable is the adjective behind the adverb.
items.exampleCN: noticeable 是这个副词背后的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Noticeably keeps the full judging sense.
items.exampleCN: noticeably 保留了完整的判断意味。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unnoticeable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unnoticeable。

items.example: Notice as a noun means an announcement.
items.exampleCN: notice 作名词时表示告示。

items.example: Notable is a near relative built with the suffix -able.
items.exampleCN: notable 是用后缀 -able 构成的近亲词。

items.example: Notably is easy to confuse with noticeably.
items.exampleCN: notably 很容易与 noticeably 混淆。
